After hearing how terrific the food and atmosphere are at Tornado Club, I was eager to try it. I had the 8 oz filet and my girlfriend had the queen of hearts burger. They were both really good, but since we were in the mood for something different I chose the shrimp and grits sandwich. It came with a side of cole slaw and was very tasty indeed! The restaurant is located in an old school part of town that was once an African American community (as well as many other ethnic groups). The town has seen gentrification and you can see that some of the original buildings have been replaced by new businesses. In spite of these changes though there is still much history here, including this one. In addition to their typical menu items they also offer "Specialty" items like smoked pork chops, fried chicken wings or fried okra. You get what you pay for at any restaurant- every item comes cooked and prepared exactly as ordered so your taste buds will always be satisfied. This particular location serves lunch and dinner and offers authentic Southern cuisine (or in other words, the same thing you'd find at Harvey's Kebab House). Prices range from 4 - 8 per meal depending on what you order.

This isn't a review of the food, just the way the business is run. I was anxious to taste their chicken schawarma and arrived about 10:55 a.m. I went to the back door behind the deli counter only to see that it had been locked for some unknown reason. After sitting in front of the locked doors for about 45 minutes, we left. I just wanted to let you know what happened after our visit. Last night's meal consisted of two pieces of Chicken Schawarma, one piece of hummus, and two slices of Tofutti Salad with dressing on the side. The portion size was small but very filling! It also included avocado chips, an order of fries and coleslaw, and two rolls with butter ketchup (one grilled roll and one non-grilled roll). The service at this restaurant was poor as well. We waited over 30 minutes before being served by a waitress who did not speak English properly. This made me feel like I was being treated like an animal. She actually didn't even ask if I needed anything when she brought us our food or what my dietary needs were. She simply said "I'll bring your food here." When asked where we ordered from, she told us, "We don't have any food here right now." When we finally got our food she attempted to charge us 5 per plate (15 total) because there wasn't enough room in her tiny office. And then proceeded to tell us our orders would take 2 weeks to be delivered. We later discovered that I had forgotten to mention that the 5 bill was only a tip for the server and that they already charged the guest a gratuity of 10 for sharing the table with them. Does anyone know why servers are expected to pay these tips? Why shouldn't the customer have to cover all the costs associated with having a table? You can get fast food for cheaper than going out to eat at SubwayChili's.
Expensive drinks, expensive to get in. It took hours for the dj we came for to even show up. Ended up leaving. Wish I could get a refund but that's not gonna happen. Damn

It is just down the street from me but as far as food goes it is just okay... The reason the rating is so low is due to the fact that I had a horrible experience at this place about 15 years ago. She never even bothered to ring up my check!!! So she obviously knew exactly how much food they ordered. And instead of getting a salad, I got broccoli! sigh My daughter who loves broccoli couldn't believe some of the things that were put onto those plates. My husband thought it was hilarious when he watched her try to eat it though LOL! We are both glad we ate there now because I don't want to do anything to mess up the family story books! One horrible thing that happened recently was that one of our friends got married! We met him around 10 years ago through mutual friends, and have been together ever since! He is absolutely wonderful! His wife was really good looking too! Something happened last Sunday night that made his wedding day not quite complete; he still hadn't consummated the marriage yet! In short, I'm pretty sure someone stole 3 different vases from the reception tables! At least we know where to start our search! Thankfully, we weren't able to break into anyone's house, but it does suck to lose those beautiful pieces that form such an integral part of your wedding decorations. As terrible as everything sounded before, at least our friends' wedding isn't ruined! How difficult can it be?! I am guessing it will take months to recover those awesome vases, especially with the amount of people attending the party! Another thing that bummed me out also was that my husband and I don't feel comfortable having strangers come hang out by ourselves at home anymore! Having relatives visit and kids hanging out with others is exhausting! Luckily, just because there are a lot of guests doesn't mean everyone knows each other very well. However, there is definitely a feeling of being constantly checked - out these days and as a single mom trying to stay focused on work and keeping the bills paid, this doesn't help either! A few weeks ago I received an email from a friend who lives a couple of hours away. Her mother called to invite her out to dinner! Of course I accepted (all I need is a little extra money for booze!), so we headed downtown to spend time with my friend's parents. The menu had several choices for drinks, including beer, wine and champagne. Since it was an adult affair, we opted for cocktails. Before ordering, the bartender asked if we would like to share. Both of us agreed and gave the server our names. After checking the numbers, she wrote down the orders we had given and handed it over without asking questions. That seemed strange to me, so once the waiter returned with the check, I began thinking about my initial reaction to the whole situation. Especially considering that my mother often takes us out at least twice a week! What made this so upsetting about the entire incident was that my friend offered to pay the tab myself. My husband usually pays for anything, whether or not it is supposed to be his responsibility, and always tells us to tip generously. To say it hurt to hear him tell me to leave the restaurant early was understatement. There was a lot of anger directed towards me throughout the evening, even when I was trying hard not to show it. I felt awful because even though I had just corrected my mistake, it took a lot longer than expected for me to be able to let it go. That's when I started remembering this conversation I used to have with my father every Thanksgiving dinner growing up. If I remember correctly, he would ask me "Are you happy?" before leaving. Whenever I answered yes, he'd reply ..." you're always happy..." Thanksgiving is always such a fun time with my family. It's nice to relax, enjoy drinks and appetizers, try new foods and catch up with other common topics of left; North east port. river native is decs outy. oO river. river

My husband and I wanted to try something new for date night and I've known about Bachi Burger for years through Yelp as one of the best burgers in Las Vegas. We decided it was time to check this place out, because we were both feeling adventurous with a little bit of veggie tension! Let's just say that Bachi is not what you would call traditional...and boy does it live up to its name. The food here is everything you'd expect from a burger joint: sweet potato fries, hot pickles, fresh herb-roasted veggies on the side...the whole nine yards! Just like most people know before they enter, there are no vegetarian options at all. (Unless you count the burger of course.) And if you don't want anything meaty, nothing quite beats the classic Southern fried chicken or bacon cheeseburger - so why bother trying something else? The prices are reasonable, since everyone knows how much vegitarian food costs these days. For appetizers; 6 a piece, half price after 6pm. Of course, our entrees came with sides galore, but let me tell ya...this place had some great stuff going on!! Everything seems to be made with love, meaning there aren't any preservatives here and each bite has that freshness you usually only get when eating home cooked items. Our faves were the french fries, which consisted of crunchy potato chips topped with melted cheese and a hint of tangy mayo; just asking for a dab of lemon butter sauce with your meal. When you add in the good portions and the stellar service, you can easily spend more than 30 prior to tip. It doesn't hurt either that their drink menu is extensive, ranging from 2.50 tea lattes to soda fountain drinks. While pricey, they're definitely worth every cent. We bought a few things, mainly because we thought it might be fun to go back later to grab more. As usual, my friend ordered a burger, while I got the New York Style hot dog (a combo of grilled onions and sauerkraut), and we shared some beer. Both items went over well, and our friends who didn't partake also enjoyed them. In conclusion, I think we'll all be coming back again soon for another visit:

Mandalay Bay does not disappoint. Although I always stay at this hotel, this past weekend we tried one night at Mirage and 2 at MB - let me tell you how the Mirage is a very different experience from MB! All in all I found this salsa to be quite delicious: thick but full bodied, mild yet flavorful, and very well balanced. I agree with other reviewers who felt like the cilantro made the salsa - it adds such a unique dimension of flavor, I can understand why people don't taste it as strongly. If anything, I think it complements the flavors of the rest of the salsa beautifully...which is something I hope more Hispanic salsas will do! There are so many great options out there when it comes to Mexican salsas; most make tons of use of herbs or added ingredients to get extra creative. Both were delicious though slightly forgettable compared to everything else. A word about dessert however-the chocolate chip cheesecake was divine. Literally the best thing ever put into a mouth. If there's anywhere near me serving something comparable, count yourself lucky. All in all I'm very excited to come back here again sometime soon because the service matches its quality 100. But sometimes my sister would come along and take me around afterward! One place our friends took us to see live entertainment recently was Brooklyn Bowl. These guys love bowling AND music - how cool?! And yes, it really looks like something straight off of Pinterest, whether its the decor, bowls full of balls ready for use while attending shows, bowls filled with fooddrink waiting for hungry patrons....who cares? NYE will be epic! Our city skyline view from Fremont Street Experience Fremont Street Experience provides nightly entertainment near the hotels casino areas down below. Different acts perform each day ranging from singers doing covers to high energy bands playing original songs. You'll find street performers walking through crowds dressed as everything imaginable; Elvis impersonators right next to acrobats balancing precariously atop poles. What makes things extra fun though is spending hours wandering sidewalks looking for photogenic spots away from the hustle and bustle underneath buildings and bridges. On rare occasions VIP guests may arrive.....these giant balloons were part of another New Year's Eve celebration. Everything seemed larger-than-life! And don't forget Downtown Summerlin either!! Here's what it looked like as fireworks flew across an incredible sky above the area last year..you couldn't ask for better views anywhere else!

Most of us who live in Las Vegas have quietly accepted the fact that restaurants on the Strip are notoriously over-priced. It used to be that Strip restaurants offered a more affordable alternative, but it's not always easy for anyone to afford them when they were priced out by the hordes living around the strip and the vast majority weren't able to find them elsewhere because Las Vegas is known as a free market town where food prices can sometimes go up or down at will without making other people pay any higher rent than they would if they had to deal with a restaurant closer to home. The result was restaurant closures across the Strip during the recession, so restaurants closed their doors as businesses shuttered due to closing chains like TGI Fridays and McDonald's. What's worse, many restaurateurs said we never saw their tables set aside because they didnt want to run out of money doing something else - baristas couldnt get jobs here since theres no money coming back from their employers. With new realities sweeping through Las Vegas, its clear restaurants need to make adjustments lest they turn into establishments that serve only whatd clearly cost too much. It is impossible to say what will happen now given a management team trying desperately to keep up with the demand.I dont know how long that will take. But there has been some progress toward revamping Las Vegas economy after decades of stagnation due largely to the citys two most popular destinations: Las Vegas Strip hotels and casinos. If hotel rooms start popping up again soon, the Strip could become a major tourist destination once again. But it wont succeed without changes helping keep restaurants afloat while providing jobs far beyond the Strips boundaries. The Strip needs to stay open longer than ever before thanks to the tourists who came to Las Vegas following the Strips rise in popularity on the Strip between 1927 and 1970. It wasnt until the 1960s that Vegas evolved into one of the wealthiest areas of the world adding quite possibly millions of jobs last year alone which created an estimated 20 million jobs throughout the decade leading up to the Great Recession. But Las Vegas isnt unique among cities experiencing dramatic job losses this year. Tourism stocks along the Strip still arent recovering quickly enough to withstand the downturn lingering around the valley. Strip properties must also adapt to rapidly changing technology trends such as airport touts and virtual tours introducing guests to other places around the world. And even though the Strip remains booming despite the pandemic, Las Vegas tourism industry should suffer greatly. Without those opportunities things remain difficult for those facing layoffs. Las Vegas needs more flexibility rather than less flexibility for its residents. The Strips assets are currently being valued heavily compared to the rest of the nations reliance on vacations. Las Vegas hotels are increasingly expensivebecause the Strip doesnt offer many options others favor. But the Strip should focus instead on attracting visitors attractions that arent immediately accessible locally. The Strips parks and museums provide a suitable place for younger generations to meet friends. Thatll continue even amid the pandemic. This sushi eatery doesn't seem expensive either since they sell their own products so you may not need fancy roll making equipment even though no matter where you go you'll get some sushi rolls unlike many people who are known for serving sushi rolls over noodles. Sunset Grill serves sushi en route back home through one of their restaurants. They include a variety of flavors ranging from puffer fish to tuna and salmon, with the vast majority going into fruit machines to create bowls stuffed with tropical fruits. Their sushi roll section houses a variety of sushi rolls together with full sides and vegetable toppings waiting for your taste buds to settle down enough for you to enjoy them yourself. They serve sushi from their buffet style tables alongside freshly caught fish balls, squid paste dipping sauces (which make perfect sushi rolls), clam chowder, pork shanks, vegetables salad and more. Sunset Grill offers sushi buffet specials every Monday and Thursday 10 am-5 pm. But be warned they don't serve sushi anymore unless you request it first. They're always busy trying to meet demand but you won't see them often since they aren't staying open till 4:30am everyday once again this week! Sunset Grill plays host to other restaurants throughout Glendale each month providing plenty of opportunities to grab snacks and drinks without paying thousands for those days.

Most of us who live in Las Vegas have quietly accepted the fact that restaurants on the Strip are notoriously over-priced. Also known as Tengu Sushi, Chef Yamamoto began his journey making sushi nearly 40 years ago at Tokyo's famous Sashimi Tsukiji Market. "The world has changed tremendously over these past four decades," he says. "Sushi received recognition from many quarters. In Japan, sushi restaurants proliferated greatly due to the popularity of popular shows featuring celebrity chef cooks preparing deluxe meals. People wanted to see celebrities prepare food instead of relying exclusively on ramen bars. Then the internet became readily accessible. Many young people wanted to share their cooking skills online - and sushi hit prime-time television screens nationwide through various videos hosted on YouTube channels. Fans could learn cuisine techniques easily via expert demonstrations posted onto video sites like Vine. Accordingly, sushi culture expanded rapidly across America over the last decade."

Most of us who live in Las Vegas have quietly accepted the fact that restaurants on the Strip are notoriously over-priced. It used to be that Strip restaurants offered a slightly elevated dining experience, justifying their prices with the promise of a glamorous environment and a stellar view. But times have changed, and so have the restaurants. I've been eating on the Strip for a decade now and I can tell you that some of the best dining experiences I've had in Las Vegas have taken place at neighborhood casinos that are within walking distance of the Strip. Most neighborhood casinos offer multiple dining options, and these dining options are often not just cheaper than Strip restaurants but also on par with or even superior to the more famous, more expensive restaurants on the Strip. And most of these restaurants don't require reservations, so you don't have to worry about planning your dining schedule weeks in advance. Of course, the Strip is still home to some of the best restaurants in Las Vegas. In the past, I've recommended many of these restaurants, including Koi, L'Atelier de Joel Robuchon, Daniel Boulud Brasserie, and Mix. But today I'd like to recommend a few Strip restaurants that are almost as good as the neighborhood restaurant, but at a lower price. Michael Mina's Bourbon Steak. This place gets a lot of attention, and with good reason. Mina has been pushing the boundaries of Vegas cuisine for years, and this is the place where he showcases his signature dishes. The menu features some of the best steaks in Las Vegas (and one of the best baked Alaskas I've ever tasted) and the wine list is consistently ranked among the top five lists in the city. You'll pay a premium for this experience, but it's worth it. Josie's at Caesars Palace. This is the place where Bradley Ogden (Ogden's, Lark Creek Inn) and Guy Savoy (Guy Savoy, and the new Brasserie at Caesars) create a more casual, less expensive alternative to their expensive restaurants. The menu is short and simple, but the flavors are authentic and the service is great. Sushi Roku at Caesars Palace. This is the place where Nobu Matsuhisa brings his Sushi Roku concept to Las Vegas. The food is served in smaller portions than at Nobu, but it is more affordable and as delicious as the Nobu food. If you're craving a sushi dinner on the Strip, this is the place to go. China Grill at the Mandalay Bay. This place gets a lot of love from my readers, and it's easy to see why. The food is exceptional and the service is great. The menu is also very diverse, with Chinese, Japanese, Thai, and Korean dishes, and I'm always happy with whatever I order. And the views are terrific. Nine Fine Irishmen at New York-New York. This is a very popular spot with the local Irish community, and it serves some of the best Irish food in Las Vegas, if not in the entire country. The menu features a variety of traditional and contemporary Irish dishes, and I always love the atmosphere. Fleur de Lys at the Mandalay Bay. I know, I know. This is supposed to be an overpriced Strip restaurant. But you have to understand that the food at this restaurant is on par with the food at Thomas Keller's Bouchon and Per Se in New York City, and the prices are often comparable. The atmosphere isn't quite as casual as the other restaurants on this list, but the food is terrific. The Strip is home to dozens of other great restaurants, including Michael Mina's American Fish, Gordon Ramsay's Verandah, the Eiffel Tower Restaurant at the Paris, the Stratosphere Buffet, and the Bacchanal Buffet at Caesars Palace. The Strip restaurants may be pricey, but they're usually worth every penny. Most of the restaurants at Caesar's Palace are great. You should try The Bacchanal Buffet, it's about 15-20 per person. Never order Mexican with a slick facade. Anyplace in a strip mall with Grandma back in the kitchen usually yields the gold. This place, all hipster glitter and low rider vintage hubcaps, was a bad idea. But it was the place I stopped in to at the last minute on the way to the airport, and their Mexican Grilled Cheese (11) looked like the sort of thing I would enjoy when I'm flying and hungry. Tender, warm, with a spicy kick, this sandwich was tasty. But the "cheese" part was a bit thin. I guess I was hoping for something more molten, but instead it was thin enough that I could taste the bread. If the cheese had been meltier it would've been a knock out. The side of guacamole (7) was pretty good, too. Rich and creamy, with some garlic, cilantro, and lime flavors. The blueberry margarita (9) was sweet and berry-y, but otherwise unremarkable. The chips and salsa, on the other hand, were pretty good, with good chunks of tomato and a smoky, spicy kick. I still think that what I really needed was a bean and cheese burrito, but sometimes you can't get what you really want, especially when it comes to Mexican food in a strip mall in a suburb. Most of us who live in Las Vegas have quietly accepted the fact that restaurants on the Strip are notoriously over-priced. It used to be that Strip restaurants offered a decent value, but now costs seem prohibitively expensive compared with quality. In a column earlier this month, we talked about how some restaurant owners were considering a price hike for their diners because they had been losing money and needed it badly Restaurant prices could jump up 15 percent or more by year's end, experts say," Nov. 3). The article mentioned that high rents were partly to blame: "While many large strip malls rent space from casinos at nominal rates, these smaller establishments pay top dollar. And while the casino gets first pick of tenants... those spots don't bring in enough revenue." The harsh reality is that there has never been any doubt among those of us living here in Southern Nevada that Strip eateries charge way too much - what one might call an obvious truth. But as I read the story, even though my husband and I rarely eat out, I was reminded why I stay away most often: We can get almost everything we need without leaving our neighborhood; if we do want something special, we don't hesitate to order takeout instead of going out. So raising prices isn't necessary to make them profitable. There must be another reason? Lately, it seems like every time we turn around, we hear about another business closing down along Sahara Avenue. Just last weekend, Amaro Restaurant closed its doors after 42 years. In September 2009, Quiubo Mexican Grill and Tequila Bar shuttered after 14 months. What's happening? Why would so many businesses fail, especially ones that seemed pretty popular when they opened? Who knows? Maybe it's just me, but lately I feel like Las Vegans are becoming complacent. Everyone assumes they'll always find work, housing will continue to appreciate and food will always be available right outside their door - no matter where you go. People are less willing to venture beyond their comfort zone than ever before. They've stopped looking at other places to see whether maybe things aren't better over there; what they really mean is "I hope nothing bad happens." That attitude stifles creativity and entrepreneurship, which makes it difficult for people who actually care about progress to thrive. If everyone thought only about themselves, Las Vegas wouldn't look nearly as appealing as it does today. So next time you complain that your favorite bar or coffee shop doesn't offer happy hour all day long, remember that someone worked hard to keep local talent afloat when times got tough. Know that whenever another place closes down, somewhere else opens up to try to give residents exactly what they're asking for: cheaper beer and bottomless mimosas.

I like to tan before vacation and had a pleasant experience tanning at Sun Tan City last year so decided to go there this year before vacation. Not sure if I could get the same tan as last time but didn't want to take any risks with my skin after all that sunscreen use already! They have various packages on offer, from 6 for one hour up to 40 for five hours. The prices include complimentary lotion spray and you can also buy additional bottles of sun protection products (e.g. SPF50) which are very reasonably priced in Singapore. There's even free wifi available too, good for checking email or uploading photos onto Facebook while your tan is setting:) We opted for the first package (15 each), which includes two 1-hour sessions. Each session begins with a consultation where they spend some time going through your skincare regime, discuss what kind of tan you're looking for etc. The room was nice - it felt clean and fresh with soft cushioned seats and nicely decorated wallsfloors. They used special UV light bulbs to ensure only the right amount of ultraviolet rays reach customer's skins during their session; however traditionally, these types of booths do emit more heat than other forms of indoor tanning such as beds. At our appointment, we were given 2 bottles of aloe vera gel to apply 10 minutes before entering the booth, plus an application form to fill out and sign for later reference. We then proceeded into the waiting area until our turn came along next door. It took about 15 minutes total between consultation filling out the application form wait time. To start off with, I got myself a quick 5 minute 'pre-tan' sesh done by one of the staff members using only the handheld device which emits far less heat compared to the larger power lamps used outdoors. This enabled me to test how tolerable it might be for people who haven't been exposed to this type of technology previously. If necessary I would simply stick to doing it indoors rather than risk overexposure to the stronger outdoor version otherwise!: Afterwards, it was time to enter the main 'booth'. It has 3 different stations: airbrush, hand gun, laser (the most powerful machine). At least four staff would help customers choose which station to use based upon their personal preference. For example, having a small zit? Filling in pores faster with the airbrush machine. Have sensitive skin? Better to just shoot some sunless tanner on, no need to worry about burning yourself due to the lower wattage. There are 4 steps in total during the whole process - cleansing, exfoliation, tanning and moisturizing. During each step, the booth will ask specific questions related to your skin tone color preferences Are you fair dark?" "How much coverage do you prefer?," etc.). Customers are reminded not to stay in the booth longer than 30 minutes at a stretch since skin gets damaged quickly under the intense UVA exposure. Overall, I liked that the treatment wasn't overly perfumed or scented and went easy on the fragrance itself. Plus, everything smelled really fresh and natural. Although personally I'm not keen on the whole cake-like appearance you end up achieving because of the ultra thin layer of tanned skin it leaves behind...and I wouldn't say those look super healthy either..hmm.

It was packed full of rowdy college students during the UNC-Duke game (and we were happy about this), but I also saw families there as well - everyone seemed pretty pumped up for some wings with extra blue cheese dressing and nachos topped with chili and jalapenos! The prices are reasonable too - under 10 per person gets you two people plenty fed. We've eaten here before several times and really enjoy their menu; it changes periodically based on what ingredients they have available, which keeps things interesting. My favorite wings are still Buffalo chicken, but macaroni cheese and garlic bread are great staples too. Their pizza isn't terrible either if you want something different from your typical wing joint. Go early because you can expect lines out into the street when there's big games being played!

I was so hopeful to find a good BBQ place. I heard great things about this place but wanted to wait until the lines went down from it being new. The food itself wasn't bad, just not worth waiting in line for over an hour and a half (over 3 hours of total time). The burgers were ok, nothing special... absolutely no one should be paying 20burger at any restaurant anymore. This is supposed to be "fast casual" fast food? Very disappointed! This is the second location opened by the same owner who also owns Fazoli's Italian Kitchen franchise: Both locations are of similar quality as many other fast-casual places like Chipotle or Five Guys, with high prices compared to local restaurants. It is not uncommon that they will charge more than half the price you would pay if ordering through their website or app. Also, unlike Chipotle, they do not offer guacamole on its own; instead, it has to be ordered along with a meal. However, even when ordering online, corn tortillas are limited to two per week, while flour tortillas can only be purchased once every four weeks. In addition, even though there may seem like endless choices available, these offerings tend to run dry during lunch rushes and weekends. On top of all of those issues, the staff tends to get overwhelmed quickly, leading to long waits and uneven service. For example, on Sunday nights around dinner rush, servers have been known to turn away customers because there simply isn't enough space to seat everyone without missing out on orders.

I told myself that on my next trip to Vegas, I was gonna try one of the nicer buffets on the Strip. My husband I stayed at Paris, and it is a pretty nice hotel but we did not know what all the fuss was about in regards to buffets here. We didn't find this one as bad as some people made them out to be. It could have been better though! But really, only because I tend towards the fancier restaurants when I go to vegas (and I can afford those in other cities). The food selection looked alright for Christmas Day, although were kind of lacking compared to years past. There are two types of salads - redgreen and potato-based with little dressings available which you mix yourself or choose from packets. The first time ever I had chicken wings there. They're ok, nothing special. Chicken strips look like they came right off the grill straight onto your plate without any marinating whatsoever. Most lack seasoning too so you need lots more sauce than usual. This goes back up a lot if you order several items instead of just one. And the jalapeno popper dip was wayyyy too spicy!!! Like I'm talking burn holes through your tongue type stuff. Not sure why they decided to add that considering most guests probably don't want their food to actually hurt their mouth. Not even sure how much they charged me since they forgot to charge us for our eggs Benedict last year...it's annoying when servers forget to charge things until after everything else has already disappeared! So yea....not impressed by these "buffets" despite having free breakfast included. When asked how many people would be eating there tonight, she seemed surprised we ordered 2 plates each..she said "oh no..usually we get 5 plates maximum for dinner." She must not work Wednesdays then!! Because I've seen quite a few families eat there alone. Maybe they do count counting kids who aren't old enough to sit still on chairs during dinners? Or maybe they just leave early? Whatever...this place needs to learn what a buffet means!!!! Even the entrees weren't very good either when comparing them to what you'd expect at more expensive places. For example: A hotdog?? Wtf??? Never heard of such a thing lolol After leaving the dining area around 10pm, security tried to stop us three times to make sure someone wasn't missing. Honestly. Some nights yeah maybe...but Christmas night?!? Call me crazy but does anyone think people come home from partying late and decide to ditch family members? No thank you. These hotels take money knowing full well everyone will pay anyway. Also, staff greeting customers with hugs and kisses while wearing skimpy outfits.....really classy NOT haha By far the worst part was being treated horribly and ignored constantly throughout dinner. Oh wait..that might have been the best part LOL

This is a very well run airport, but the security line can get way too long. The food choices in the terminals is just ok. Nothing to write home about (but nothing bad either). I love this place and will always fly out of SFO when I visit San Francisco again!

Worst place to go for medical care. Had me waiting for two hours for test results than when I finally get seen, I get the oh, we need to get you into emergency room right away because of this problem or that problem.. blah blah Dang... That's awful! You should complain about the wait time (and late diagnosis) and maybe even call a lawyer in case it was malpractice on their part

Even if you have been to a Bashas'markets Inc before, you must go to this one! You could spend hours here, eat dinner, have a drink, and shop. Obviously the food is very good (we're talking about Buffalo chicken wraps). They also sell their own brand of items that are not availablenot sold anywhere else in town. I highly recommend going on Sundays for the best deals. The store was packed with people at 10 am on Sunday morning making it hard to find parking spaces but I didn't mind because there were such great bargains to be had. Also make sure your coupons match up exactly as some stores will check them or charge more than they should.

I really try to be understanding about food taking some time. I am very willing to wait for quality food. Its actually my tagline for yelp...however, this place takes too damn long and you can't even get a burger in 3 hours when they open at 11am-1pm because of construction. If you are up early enough go across the street to Stroube's instead! Also if you have more patience than methe burgers Burger Bar will be better after a few weeks or months with all the ingredients finding their places on the grill.

Simple, well prepared food. Good atmosphere, good service. Heavier and more traditional than the meal we had at Bouillon Bilk the night before. Food was very good quality for a reasonable price (around 10 euros per person). Strongly recommended if you are looking for something different and interesting to eat in Paris - though it's not cheap! On our last day of exploring Paris as tourists and eating my way through this wonderful city I finally found somewhere that really blew me away....Its called La Mere Brazier! Its located on Rue St. Honore in the 8th Arrondissement...The interior is beautiful!! The lighting with candles burning all over trimmings from old French furniture just adds so much to the ambiance. In addition there were some incredible pieces of art scattered around...Old paintings painted by some famous artists like Picasso which have been reproduced onto canvas or wooden walls etc.. It seems they change out what they have displayed here each month, but its always consistent with current trends of course; There was also quite an extensive wine list available and we ordered two bottles of Chateauneuf du Pape Rose because why not??: The main thing about this place however was not evident until we actually tried their meals!!! They serve up truly authentic vintagetraditional french cuisine...with an added kick or two depending on how adventurous you fancy being:) We started off with this delicious starter consisting of chicken liver pate served with truffle toast points. For mains we chose Beef wellington (which came with gravy) and Gratin Dauphinois (creamy potato dish)...I couldnt believe how real these dishes tasted...They even offer RICE with your meal!!!! Oh yes!!! And dont forget dessert either.....We opted for Chocolate cremeux (chocolate flowing cream) accompanied by chocolate sauce. All three courses were absolutely exquisite........Ohhh and did i mention 20 europp inclusive of drinks??? Well get yourselves down to Rue St.Honore No8 Apt 5B!!!;)

Food is decent. I ordered a stuffed trout dinner entree. Looks pretty good, a little bit cold. It was quite busy, which explains why they never fill up my glass of wine. That's OK though because it wasn't empty for long. They do have a nice selection of beers and wines on tap, but the service isn't great when you are seated so far from the bar area where people who get water or want another drink order them. There is also no menu at this location. This place has been around forever. Not much to say other than that. You can bring your own beer into their pub or give them 2pint if you don't feel like lugging it in yourself (they open at 11am). No food here; just drinks 5 plates off a small menu with about 15-20 items total. The crowd is mostly regulars who talk amongst each other across the table. One thing to remember: no reservations allowed! A fun addition would be the inclusion of karaoke nights once every month.

Never order Mexican with a slick facade. Anyplace in a strip mall with Grandma back in the kitchen usually yields the gold. This place, all hipster glitter and low rider coolness is not it. I lived near there for years but only went once about 5-6 years ago when they first opened... I remember being sorely disappointed: (They definitely didn't have much of an interior to speak of though so maybe that has changed?

We will not go back!! The ribs looked big and meaty but were tough. The Mac n cheese was dry and no flavor potato salad was the same. The pulled pork sandwich had a lot of fat on it, looked like bacon actually... The food here is good if you want your tastebuds to be blasted into oblivion. I won't return!!!

I would give Ginza 0 stars if I could! This was truly the worst dining experience I have ever had. My husband took me to Ginza for my birthday. Upon arrival, we were told that there was a 60-minute wait and it was too expensive so they could not provide us with a table. We stood in line for an hour waiting on our food which wound up taking more than two hours because of their incompetence serving lines at one time after another. The "several course tasting menu" did not include any appetizers or desserts nor included any drinks or water with your meal. Our waiter was very unfriendly and rude as well. When you are paying 500 per person for dinner, this is unacceptable behavior from staff members who should be trained properly.

Stayed here in the spa suite for three nights. At first glance it looks swanky, but after spending half an hour in the room, you start to notice all these small details and flaws that really make this place less than ideal if not downright nasty.... Read MoreLess By javiergjv The hotel is nice at night when all lights are on. But during day time its dark with bright lighting, which can be a bit annoying sometimes because of reflections from windows or glass doors. The interiors need...

I got the veggie pad Thai- it was out of this world good. The tofu was delicious and the meal was chock full of vegetables. I love that they ask you what kind of spice level you want instead of guessing like most places do now when making meals, (my preference is medium to high). It's a great place for lunch or dinner with friends!

I bought Panda show ticket, Vegas.com stated that it comes with Gondola ride voucher but I didn't get the voucher and wasted few hours of my short vacation. At first, I thought they'd lock me out when all shows were sold-out completely, they must have recorded our names. They let us in without any problems later though. Panda was great as always - best thing is to enjoy the music while floating on a gondola!We made reservations which we are glad about now (this year) because you can't just walk up anymore..

Great beer selection, of course. Had the Pork Belly sandwich and found it a bit too fatty, but taste was good. Their Potted Farm Egg appetizer was really good. Very busy on Friday night with lots of young couples out for the weekend in town. It's very hard to find somewhere that is still open at 11pm; this place definitely fits the bill! They have an absolutely amazing beer list that changes every couple months (as well as rotating beer from other places). I had the Rogue Hazelnut Brown Nectar which tasted fantastic - don't miss out if you love beer! The food here is pretty decent too - I'd say the best part about the whole experience though is the friendly staff. Everyone who works there seems genuinely happy to be working there- It has such a great atmosphere!

Never really had a problem with this chipotle But had a terrible experience today. Employees were super rude from start to finish. Awful customer service. The lady at the end tried her best but was obviously stressed out and annoyed I'm always nice when I go there, even though their food is pricey. Maybe it's just that people are in bad moods on Mondays?

Siri took me here.... Take me to the closest Cigar Shop. I discovered there was so much more to this awesome inquiry! Walked into a Cigar experience. Pretty pretty nice.... I have been smoking for 8 years and have never seen anyone ask Siri for directions anywhere, but in relation to cigars? Where is it that you live?!

I was excited to find a sushi place near our home in Glendale, but the excitement faded as soon as I walked in to the place. It has a very outdated feel and you know it's been there for many years with all of its needs updating (seating space is currently limited due to renovations). The food itself wasn't bad though- appetizers were decent and the lox on bagel sandwich tasted pretty good! The best part about this Japanese restaurant would have to be the prices, which are much lower than other area restaurants that serve similar food quality - such an awesome deal!!! You can get your meal plus dessert or a drink for under 15!! Plus they deliver too if you don't want to leave the house:) They also offer catering services so feel free to call them for some great take out!

Really, you guys think chips should be the basis of a good or bad rating????? wow how about the actual food, the real meal, not the free stuff in front of the cash register. I was commenting on your first comment... I don't care for chips either but it's just another way to rate and get an idea if people like what they are buying

I really enjoyed my stay here. The entire property is very hip and comfy. The rooms are large with cool decor. The restaurant, Cafe ZuZu, serves great food and drinks. If you like to have a drink at night then they serve free happy hour Monday through Friday from 6pm-7:30pm! At the end of our day in Santa Barbara we went for dinner on their rooftop with a view over the ocean (and that's where I took these photos!).

This is a different type of dining experience. From the outside, it looks like an ordinary building, but the inside is nicely decorated. Wines selections are great. Staff are super friendly and welcoming. We had dinner there last night with friends for birthday celebrations. The place was very busy when we went at 8pm but that's fine because service very fast! Would def go back again!! Food: 910 Value For Money: 1010 Ambience: 55

I omitted to mention that the attitude stemmed from the fact that we did not have a local number, just the hotel's phone number. Apparently that was a problem for them too as they were unable to reach us using only one of their phones (which would make sense if it happened during business hours). We also noticed on our return trip there seemed an abundance of taxis shuttling about at all times and wondered why? If people are staying in hotels then surely they need to get around so where do these drivers earn their money after dropping you off at your destination? That was probably what made me ask my initial question above!
Happy to have a Jersey Mikes in Surprise, AZ. Been here 4 times and the have never disappointed! This location is extremely busy Yet, they are very good at working with you on your order.

My wife and I had breakfast here on a Monday morning before our flight home. We got seated immediately and had fast, happy service, and that's where the enjoyable portion of my experience ended! The food was terrible (or at least it was for me), even though we ordered off their "special" menu with fresh ingredients. It looked like someone took some good ingredients from a local farmer market or something along those lines and put them in a microwave to reheat them. My omelette was completely burned inside - not just poorly cooked but ruined completely by being overcooked to the point where there were blackened bits all over the top and bottom of every single piece of egg - plus when I asked if they could cook mine half-way between medium and well done so as not to burn everything outside while leaving enough uncooked yolk in the center to make the eggs runny, I received an extremely rude response from one of the staff members who told me I needed to specify exactly how I wanted it cooked before ordering any more food because apparently she couldn't read minds or tell what kind of person we both are based upon conversation alone. Also, despite asking for no salt added to my coffee - which is normally free refills anyway - I still wound up paying 2 extra after having already paid 3 for the drink itself (and you know what else? She actually charged ME less than her coworker did next door!). The coffee tasted fine without much creamsugar since I'm used to drinking it that way at home anyways; this place charges almost twice as much per ounce as Starbucks does...ouch! Lastly, after being given the bill and seeing just how much extra money I'd spent compared to how little the food cost us, my wife stormed out midmeal with only about 1 bite left in her plate and gave me the middle finger salute as we walked away, refusing to pay anything beyond the price of the meal since we weren't going to eat anything else anywhere near Washington DC just before flying back to California. Needless to say, I'm glad that'll be the last time I set foot in that building ever again.

First time! After asking some fellow YELPERS where do I go... they didnt point me in the wrong direction! the place is small. but I like that. makes me feel special - nessy I ordered a black coffee and it was good, not as strong as I thought it would be though which i liked. The food came out quick enough for my liking and I enjoyed myself here at this location.

You got to get their carnitas grilled cheese with each bite, you know it was made out of love! The carnitas is so good, the melted cheeses delicious, and the tortillas are soft. Yum!! I had a chance this weekend to eat at this local spot called, El Verano de Oro (The Golden Summer). I have been wanting to try them for some time now after seeing pictures on Instagram by my friend mrskathleenlouise. We thought we would give it a go and see what all the hype was about. So far, it has met our expectations as one of the best meals in Austin thus far. We ordered an assortment of tacos and quesadillas first off which were excellent and prepared perfectly. Their margarita's are great too - not overly sweet, but just right. I also tried a couple shots, they were niiiceeee!!! They offer online ordering through GrubHub if that helps anyone else decide where to order from. All around; delicious food, friendly staff (even took care of us when we forgot something), reasonable prices, best experience yet here. Can't wait for lunch tomorrow.

I don't usually write reviews but today I decided this place was worth one:) I just got the 12 piece chicken meal for the family and I have to say, it's a little bit of heaven. The food is delicious! They also offer free refills on drinks pop which is nice. The best part about this restaurant is that you can bring your own wine or beer with no corkage fee (they do charge for ice though). They really make dining at home convenient for those days when you're not feeling up to going out - especially if we've had guests over. At our house, my husband will either grill something or fry some wings while enjoying a glass of his favourite red. He doesn't want to go to the trouble of finding another bottle in the fridge if he finishes ours off early so having the option here saves us money too since buying him another bottle would be expensive anyway.:)
This is a sad place. The dolphins are in tiny pools, and I just left sad and depressed. I'm sorry I ever came. What makes you say that? What were the conditions like when you visited?

Very poor customer service at the United airline ticket counter. I arrived at 10:45 am only one customer in front of me, 6 agent's avoiding eye contact with me. When it was my turn to check-in they told me that there were no flights so i had to wait an hour for a flight. They could not find any information about this on their computer? Most people are waiting around 2 hours before boarding time and what do you say to those who have been waiting over 4 hrs because of system errors??? I don't know how these place stay open! Perhaps you should consider closing your business because if this is customer service then customers are better off without it!!! What kind of example are you setting for other companies?

Tried to give this best buy another chance but ran into a very consistent lack of customer service. Witnessed several others very frustrated with the lack of help! The merchandise was not in good condition either and will have returned for credit or exchange today!

Just moved to the area and have never had a Bashas store in our Phoenix area. I have never encountered such rude and uncaring checkers in my life. I will not return even if they do their job right - which they obviously did not, or else there would be no complaints. I am tired of these rude people working at this location! They are always very hateful when you go into their line for help. The employees need some training also. These people think that because they work at Bashas they can get away with anything! It's really sad: (
Oreo Frozen Hot Chocolate is great! Get 3 of them! I love their red velvet cake and cheesecake, but the flavor just doesn't match with the rest of my family. I'm going to try this one though

Wife an I was there last night, the band was playing they were so so, but the people that were there were dancing and having fun...So we thought this looked nice. A woman is trying to catch a small child who has run off into traffic while her husband records it on his cellphone instead of helping. Shocking parenting from these idiots....

Very boring pizza, if you don't like garlic, oregano, any spices, and think ketchup is pretty good then this is the spot for you. Forget about putting on peppers or onions because they will just get taken off at checkout...

Changed the way I feel about Thai food! Definitely spicier than expected, but really fresh veggies and loved the tofu option for all dishes! Staff was friendly, they were just understaffed on a busy weekend night.

What a hidden gem this place is for the locals...!) CHEAP cheap freakin' CHEAP!!! My brother, G-ma (that's short for the Grandma), and myself ate a fantastic breakfast for 21! dollars. The food was hot fresh, and the service was quick but not rushed). I recommend that you go to Long John Silver's - if they have it there. If not then definitely try their fish tacos. (I'm sure the spelling will be corrected later.) This review can also be found at my sister blog:

Great ice cream however service was poor. I was number 3 in line and the cashier just wanted to chat with everybody. When my turn came around she told us there were no bananas for our smoothies then proceeded to tell another customer that they had a lot of them, when this wasn't true at all. Maybe if we weren't her last till 10:00 p.m., but on top of that she also didn't have any chocolate syrup. So instead of serving me, or returning later (we waited about 5 minutes) she then packed up everything behind the counter without saying anything. She seemed very rude overall!

Interesting experience. Our server was the sweetest thing who dealt with the mix of people on an afternoon where developmentally disabled people (seriously, no joke) demanded a lot of attention. I thought all servers were like that and if she wasn't so nice as to deal with it then we'd have been in trouble! This is worth mentioning because when you hear about "The Help" you only get to see the racism but not the help they provide for each other in their community or how much better off these women are after living there despite being abused by white men during segregation... which makes this film even more painful.

wow! What a surprise this resto was for me. I have been to the Outback on Sunset and Green Valley and do not remember it to be anything like this place. The service level, wine list, glasses...all were wonderful!!! We started with an appetizer of oysters that were cooked perfectly with some sort of tempura-like coating - perfect texture!! Then we had our first course which included pan seared scallops served over a bed of sauteed spinach....delicious! For entrees, my husband went Japanese (he is big into sushi) while I chose their roasted chicken breast with cheesy polenta cake. My daughter got mac cheese made with her favorite - penne pasta. She also ordered fries topped with bacon. They all enjoyed everything very much. Desserts are phenomenal too. A great experience overall and highly recommended.

Craft cocktails are always a welcome treat. Craft cocktails served by a cool waitressbartender are even better. Craft cocktails served by a cool waitressbartender while listening to awesome music is arguably the best craft cocktail experience of all time, at least in my book. Well meet up with me and some fellow bloggers on Thursday, November 20th for an event that has been dubbed "A Night Out In Memphis" and hosted by The Daily RFT! We will be attending Goner Records release party for new album from Anthony Crawford entitled I Thought It Was Worth A Shot (Side One).

Meh Greek Restaurant. Don't get me wrong, it wasn't bad. It was no Z's Greek on Indian School, but it wasn't bad. I had the Gyro Platter. The Greek salad and fries were pretty good too. I hate that place with a passion

We always try to stop here when saying downtown. Good food and friendly service. Love the chips and bean dip. Steak fajitas are plentifully, enchiladas are great, and the margaritas ... Yum! Great place for a date night or good friends get together. I like how it's kind of a dive with character (not fancy). I have been going there since they opened in 2000 my family loves this restaurant best prices around we go every chance we can get,the Margarita is awesome always fresh and hot no other places do that let alone homemade salsa. The corn beef hash browns are amazing everything on their menu is delicious very nice atmosphere i would recommend everyone check them out thank you so much

I would rather eat cardboard than the Pad Seu and the complimentary wings did not make the delivery. The white rice was delicious, but then my 4 year old neice started puking so we had to leave before finishing our meal.

My husband and I went here on a Saturday night at about 9:30pm. It was not very busy but it was so loud, it was ridiculous. There were two bands playing that evening from what we could hear (and our minds are pretty sharp) both of them sounded like they had no idea how to play their instruments... one band had a guy singing who seemed to think he needed an electronic device hooked up to his voice box to sound good (I would have won the lottery before buying this thing!) The other band tried many times during the evening, in vain, to imitate jazz music - another instrument for me! The food is ok if you don't mind greasy pub grub type fare. And the prices? 12.95 per person plus tax and tip which comes out to approximately 19.00. We will never go back there again......ever!

The place stinks of smoke like when it was the Imperial. The rooms are tiny. The WIFI works about half the time or less. The casino area is small, the rest is empty. Although you get a lot for your money (9night) I would recommend staying elsewhere as there are many better options in town.

Well it didn't start off too good. We were not served for some time even though it did not seem busy. It was hot but there were a few tables in the shade so we sat at one of them and ordered drinks and food when they came around to take our order. The waiter forgot about us several times, which is why I gave him only 3 stars (I lowered his rating because he also took forever getting our food). However, once he got us our glasses filled with ice water that had been sitting out on our table while waiting for nearly an hour, he redeemed himself by taking decent care of us from then on and made sure everything came out quickly without mistakes or complaints. The waitress who came over during our wait could have been more friendly towards her customers as she seemed annoyed much of the time although it's possible she just wasn't used to dealing with a large group like this. She did bring our food out pretty fast however after being seated. But that would be my biggest complaint. Even if you go here knowing ahead of time what kind of place it will be, expect to stand outside in line before entering the restaurant. Other than that, it's a nice spot to eat lunchdinner in Harlem where people can walk up for their first meal instead of having to drive somewhere else.

Beautiful decor. One of my favorite salads. Avacadoe on the bottom, stocked with Greens, with a crunchy top. For an Entree I love the Lasagna and the Osu Buco (forgive me spelling). My DD loves their Fish Tacos as well.

After hearing how terrific the food and atmosphere are at Tornado Club, I was eager to try it. I had the 8 oz filet and my girlfriend had the queen cut pork chop with a side order of green beans that were to die for (and she's not much into veggies). The steak came out great! It was so tender, juicy and flavorful! My sides were also good, but nothing special; however, our waitress brought us free dessert and coffee even though we didn't ask for them - they just happened to be offered as part of her service. We couldn't have been happier. Great place for date night or happy hour! From our review: "When comparing this restaurant's steakschops to Pappas Grill Steakhouse, which is located down the street from Tornado club on Tropicana Avenue, we found that Tornado Club has less flavor in their meat than Pappas Grill."

This isn't a review of the food, just the way the business is run. I was anxious to taste their chicken schawarma and arrived about 10:55 a.m. I went to the counter where they are supposed to be served from 11-11:30 a.m. There were already dozens of people waiting there as well and it appeared that no one had ordered any shawarmas yet. The guy behind the counter said I could order now if he can find me in line for it, but apparently his register wasn't working properly so up until then everyone who came after us at least got our number and ID written down on paper before we left; however when we returned he still hadn't found my name or order. He didn't seem too concerned though (this was around lunchtime), saying "It's not important right now...I'll try to get you your food by 1 p.m." The thing is this despite all the talk about how VIP customers have priority service, what I saw is basically an office supply store with folding tables set up agains the wall. As far as customer service goes - A. The staff seemed pleasant enough although obviously overwhelmed. But yeah, give them some money upfront because like everything else in life, sometimes things work out better for you than others..

Expensive drinks, expensive to get in. It took hours for the dj we came for to even show up. Ended up leaving. Wish I could get a refund but that's just how it goes sometimes Yeah, they gave out free shots at one point so it wasn't all bad but still pretty disappointing

It is just down the street from me but as far as food goes it is just okay... The reason the rating is so low is due to the fact that not everything works. I have had multiple problems with this place and still nothing has been fixed or replaced. It's pretty much a complete joke at this point! I used to like going there when they first opened, however over time things went downhill fast unfortunately: (People complained about them being closed too late on weeknights for example and they promised they would be opening earlier in the morningafternoon next year.... Well guess what? They are now even later than their previous closing times!! Way back before they were open 7-10PM most nights of the week and sometimes only until 5PM during peak season!! (As an aside: I think people should be allowed to close business hours whenever they want and if you don't like it then go somewhere else!) Anyway, both my husband myself agree that we've seen almost no improvement whatsoever since last summer despite many complaints and promises. We will NOT return anytime soon - maybe ever again actually.:sad::mad:

First impression of Kaba Curry was not good. Our little family walked in an hour and a half before closing and all we saw was a HUGE group of guys , drinking beer on their way to the toilets! There is no alcohol served at the restaurant but why not have it outside so you can just walk out with your drink when needed? It's disappointing that there are no tables for two or four people as well..... Not sure if you know this about curry: When it gets cold, it tastes like warm tomato ketchup....not hot (which I guess might be unappealing to some people). The food itself wasn't bad though...the staff were very nice and friendly and had they been able to use the outdoor space I'm sure the experience would've been much better. We will probably try again because even though Kaba doesn't do anything particularly special, they do lots of things really simply which seems appealing to me:)

Came here for my birthday which was on a Wednesday in March. The weather was beautiful and breezy. There were some people but there were many open tables so we didn't have to wait at all! It was great because you could get everything without having to worry about the price or waiting forever (like at Cheesecake Factory). My favorite is definitely their chicken sandwich, it's amazing. Also great deals are offered for different types of food like beer and wine vs normal price. You get what you pay for though - make sure you read up online reviews about how good certain portions are compared to other restaurants offering similar items. It's pretty hot stuff honestly and some people just aren't used to spicy foods. Overall, very yummy burger friendly staff will visit again.

Most of us who live in Las Vegas have quietly accepted the fact that restaurants on the Strip are notoriously over-priced. It used to be that Strip restaurants offered a huge discount to locals, but in recent years those discounts have greatly diminished. So when we heard that Strip restaurants were reducing their prices for a few hours on Tuesday and Wednesday nights, our reaction was: What's the catch? On behalf of all Las Vegas locals, I had to find out. I called several restaurants on the Strip and asked about their new, happy hour pricing. The menus I saw ranged from 4 appetizers and 5 drinks at Tao (which has been doing this for a while) to 8 cocktails and 6 sliders at Miller's Ale House located at New York-New York. Tao, located at the Venetian, has been offering reduced prices on food and drinks during their happy hour since they opened in 2005. "We've always had an awesome happy hour," said James Wood, director of operations at Tao. "We offer 50 percent off select appetizers, sushi rolls and cocktails." Tao has extended its happy hour times, now running from 5 p.m.-9 p.m. every Tuesday and Wednesday. "I think it will bring in more locals," Wood said. "It gives them a chance to experience what Tao has to offer without breaking the bank." When I spoke with Miller's Ale House, I learned that their happy hour is not only new, but exclusive to locals. "We are offering these deals for locals because we want them to come in and try us out," said David Clements, director of operations for Miller's Ale House. "We are priced competitively with other restaurants." Their happy hour is offered from 3 p.m.-7 p.m. every Tuesday and Wednesday. The best part of Miller's happy hour is that it includes free parking. When you show your Nevada driver's license at the hostess stand, you get two hours of free parking. If you go to most of the garages on the Strip, it will cost you close to 20. And if you want to stay longer than two hours, it's only 3 extra. The next place I called was the Hash House A Go Go at The Linq Hotel. This restaurant is known for its gigantic portions. They are also known for being pricey, so my interest was piqued when I saw the menu. For 5, you can order Chicken Fried Chicken Sliders and for 4, you can get a slice of pie. The rest of their happy hour menu ranges from 2-6, which means you could order a beer, chicken fried steak and a slice of pie for less than 15. Not too shabby. The Hash House happy hour runs from 4 p.m.-7 p.m. every Tuesday and Wednesday. In addition to the above mentioned restaurants, there are others around town who are offering special happy hour pricing for locals. These include Stripburger, Nacho Daddy, Smash Burger and Pink Taco, just to name a few. With the rise of culinary tourism in Las Vegas, the Strip restaurants are trying to lure locals back to the resorts in hopes that they will spend money elsewhere. It's a nice gesture, although over time it may be difficult to maintain. If you're looking for some great deals on food and drink on the Strip, head out to any of the above-mentioned places and enjoy!

Never order Mexican with a slick facade. Anyplace in a strip mall with Grandma back in the kitchen usually yields the gold. This place, all hipster glitter and low rider music, looked like it might be a con. But their single-minded focus was on the burrito, and we were rewarded with a simple but delicious mix of beans, rice and green chile chicken wrapped in a soft tortilla. Also try: El Taco Veloz in Salem (1125 Liberty St NE) for the excellent super burrito, or El Barrio for a real taste of Mexico City, just down the street from El Mexican restaurant (283 Division St). Taqueria Estrella Where: 1625 Commercial St NE Cost: 2.50burrito Rating: Also try: La Esperanza Taqueria Food Carts (next to El Burrito Loco), La Taqueria Nueve, La Jarochita (on Hawthorne Blvd), Alma Guadalupana (on SE 82nd, near Powell), and La Bonita Taqueria (on 82nd, near Holgate). A good burrito is hard to find. But if you know what to look for, these places make it easy. Keep your eye on the tortilla. It should be soft, not dry or hard. The ingredients should be warm and moist, not dry or old. It should be filled with enough meat and vegetables to be assertive without being overwhelming. And it should be served up promptly. Order your burrito at a taqueria, and it will likely come wrapped in foil, which helps keep it warm until you get it home. But eat it quickly; it's better fresh. Also, don't order a large burrito. A small or regular is enough for one person. The burrito is actually a fairly recent creation. Legend has it that the burrito was invented around 1900 by a restaurant owner named Juan Mendez in the town of Ciudad Juarez, just across the border from El Paso, Texas. Mendez used a donkey as his mode of transportation, and he wrapped his wares in a flour tortilla to keep them warm. He began calling it a "little donkey." But many scholars believe this story is apocryphal. Others say the burrito was created by a man named Alioto, who sold burritos from the back of a wagon in northern Mexico. This story is also suspect, because Alioto was born 15 years after Mendez's place opened. Still others think the burrito was born in southern California in the 1930s, when Mexican immigrants started opening taquerias there. The theory goes that the burrito was introduced to Californians by migrant workers, who wrapped their meals in tortillas to keep them warm while they worked in the fields. The term "burrito" was coined by Californians in the 1940s. But the most likely origin of the burrito lies in Sonora, Mexico. In the 1850s, the United States annexed half of Mexico and annexed it as a territory. A few years later, the Gadsden Purchase gave the US more land in present-day Arizona and New Mexico. As a result, thousands of Mexicans were forced to leave their homes and move north. These migrants brought their food with them, and burritos were among the dishes they took with them. Some of the earliest mentions of the burrito appeared in the early 20th century. In 1925, an article in the San Antonio Express described a dish called a "burrito" made of rolled beef, onions and beans wrapped in a flour tortilla. Another article from 1929 described a burrito as a fried tortilla stuffed with various fillings. In the 1930s and 1940s, the popularity of Mexican food spread beyond the Southwest. Burritos became popular in Southern California, where they were often served with a side of refried beans. By the 1950s, burritos had become a staple of Tex-Mex cuisine. Today, burritos are a staple of Mexican and American cuisine, and they can be found in almost every part of the country.

I'm a spicy kind of guy in general. I love bold, intense, exotic spices. Those aren't the kind you find on typical grocery store shelves. That poses a dilemma perhaps? The dilemma isn't necessarily with the intensity of the spices themselves. It's more about how to find them and then how to use them. When it comes to finding spices, your best bet is probably to head to a specialty market or an ethnic grocery store. These places are likely to have a much wider selection of spices than your typical grocery store, and they'll also be fresher and more potent. Once you've got your hands on some great spices, the next step is to figure out how to use them. That's where things can get a little tricky. If you're not used to cooking with strong spices, it's easy to go overboard and end up with a dish that's too spicy to enjoy. That's why it's important to start slowly and add the spices a little at a time until you get the flavor you're looking for. It's also a good idea to pair strong spices with other ingredients that can help tone them down. For example, if you're using a really intense spice like habanero pepper, you might want to balance it out with some sweet fruits or vegetables. With a little experimentation, you'll soon find the perfect balance of spices for your taste buds. And once you've got that down, you'll be able to create all sorts of amazing dishes that are packed with flavor.

Most of us who live in Las Vegas have quietly accepted the fact that restaurants on the Strip are notoriously over-priced. It used to be that Strip restaurants offered a level of service and quality that justified the high prices. I think we've reached a tipping point, however, and it's time to say that, when it comes to food, it's time for the Strip to go back to school. If you've been to the new Las Vegas City Hall, you know that the place is a fabulous combination of high-tech and eco-friendly. The walls are covered with super-efficient insulation, the floors are made of a composite of recycled tires, and there's even a bank of solar panels on the roof. There's a great food court on the first floor, with six different types of food. If you're feeling fast food-y, you can get a burger or tacos. If you're feeling fancy, you can go for a plate of pasta. Even the food court has been designed with eco-consciousness in mind. All the food packaging is made from corn starch, which means it biodegrades within a month of being thrown away. The food court is also a great place to people-watch. The diverse crowd at City Hall is a great representation of the many different people who make up our community. You'll see local office workers, politicians, cops, and maintenance workers all mixing it up in the food court. When I was last there, I saw a woman dressed in full-on business attire, and a guy in a full-length black leather coat. She was eating a salad, and he was eating a chili dog. I saw a guy with a deep, booming voice carrying a big black binder and wearing a red tie. He had a couple of kids with him, and they were dressed up like it was their first day of school. So, whether you want to eat some yummy food, see the future of green building, or just watch some great people-watching, be sure to visit the City Hall food court.

I was craving macaroni and cheese one day and a friend recommended this place. I wasn't impressed on my first visit, but decided to give it another try. The macaroni and cheese is very good, including the melted butter almond sauce (which I actually have no idea how to cook, so it's not something that I've ever tried) which makes for some pretty sweet bread. It also has great flavor, with fig and vanilla sweetness added. The other thing about Macaroni and Cheese is the avocado. This is always my next stop when we go out for lunch or dinner. All of my friends enjoy eating there too, and as you get closer to our home we'll probably stop by.:) On the way back home from the trip, I had an ad in the local paper saying "This restaurant will be open until 11:00 pm." I didn't think much about that at first, but after looking into their menu, i figured they would give me the option of ordering them all beforehand, even if it meant just giving them the choice of cooking things themselves instead of buying them. They did offer a 40 discount on the food, so i thought i'd share! It turns out that there are two options: order a whole mozzarella, or cut down on the veggie portions and use the extra veggies for the sides. If a lot of people like the veggie portion more than the beef or chicken, they can get up to 15 off when ordering the side. If everyone likes the beef instead, they can get 30 off when using the veggie portion. However, if you like the ramen bowl version, you could save 20. So far, no one seems to mind throwing that amount in the mix while still saving money:). If you're hungry, you can also add spinach or kale, each serving measuring 7g. Day 2: Lunch After breakfast I was soon getting used to the feel of the restaurant, especially since we visited Panera Bread last week - good quality, unfiltered fruit and veggies, but with a little filling. We ate a few bowls of burgers and fries before heading over to the BB for some coffee and some snacks. If you're looking for a quick snack during your stay here, this is definitely right for you.

Most of us who live in Las Vegas have quietly accepted the fact that restaurants on the Strip are notoriously over-priced. It used to be that Strip restaurants offered a bit more than just fine dining, but now? Not so much. The new Millennium Biltmore is home to only four restaurants - two buffets and two sit down eateries. They're all rather expensive by any measure, but the cheapest option is priced at 32person for lunch or dinner (that comes out to about 1 per person). The most expensive? A Caesar salad with pasta and soup will set you back well north of 40. That may sound like a small price difference until you realize that I had 2 people to feed... or perhaps 3 if we want Chinese takeout instead. Regardless, it doesn't make sense! And here's where the blame lands: Millennium Biltmore claims these prices are comparable to other premium hotels such as Caesars Palace. Of course they do because Caesars Palace is a luxury resort while The Millenium is not. There isn't a single hotel room within walking distance of this place except somewhat less luxurious ones at the Planet Hollywood Resort Casino. If anyone knows anything about the properties around the Biltmore Hotel, then you know there simply aren't many places nearby that cost half what the Millenia charges for a meal. Although Walt Disney was born in Chicago, his goal has always been to create "Disneyland in the desert." So with that, everything he designed for the park were meant to look and feel very California. This translates into the food: California cuisine which means mostly seafood dishes. On their website, they claim that "everything on our menus is fresh prepared daily." However, the quality of the fish slices that come off the boat looks nothing like the photos on their site. We found that some items tasted really good, others nothing special, and others downright nasty. In general, the experience at The Millenia wasn't bad, it was just disappointing given how much the food costs. We ended up eating at this location twice. But all the staff seemed pretty bored during both visits, which made me think: don't expect them to go above and beyond.
