Even if you have been to a Bashas'markets Inc before, you must go to this one! You could spend hours here, eat dinner, have a drink, and shop. Obviously the store is not just for shopping as there are huge eating areas with table service that serve everything from Mexican food; burgers, pizza, hotdogs, sushi, Chinese; seafood (they even make their own fresh pasta); sandwiches including Italian subs and Cuban wraps, soups, salads, cakes, pies; baked goods including breads, cookies, muffins, etc.; desserts, drinks (beerwine), ice creamfrozen yogurt; snacks such as chips-cheetos, popcorn, pretzels, nuts, gummi bears, candy; lots of specialty food items such as meatballs marinara sauce, stuffed shells, pita pockets, baking mixes, cheese sauces, quesadillas, tortilla soup cups, tamales, refried beans....the list goes on...and it's all homemade using only high quality ingredients!! You should also check out their bakery counter or "Bakery Bar." They bake almost every day, so they always have something new to offer. There are several different cake selections including carrot cake, black forest cake (my favorite), chocolate chip cookie dough, double fudge brownies, and red velvet cake!!! The best part about the Bakery Bar though? It serves coffee, iced tea, soft drinks, and alcoholic beverages which means your kids can get an adult beverage too! Another amazing thing about their Bakery Bar (that we do NOT recommend trying) are the cupcakes! You will find tons of varieties like lemon poppy seed, almond breeze, s'mores, butterscotch, buttercream, birthday cake, and most other flavors..all made fresh daily. If you're looking for something sweet to snack on in between meals, these will be sure to satisfy. The Souper Salad Counter was also very impressive! Not only did we love our meal at Bashas', but we were floored by our salad bar experience. For 7.99, you receive 2 big bowls full of delicious vegetables, fruits, chicken strips, and drizzled with oil and vinegar. We got strawberries, cucumbers, carrots, celery sticks, curly fries, fried shrimp chips, jalapenos, peppers, tomatoes added to our salad. It was an extremely filling meal, especially when paired with some breadsticks. We highly encourage you to stop into the large supermarket inside, where you'll find more than 40,000 products ranging in price from 89 cents to 6.99 per item!! You can buy anything from groceries to clothing to electronics..... almost any product imaginable is available within the market. As you enter through the doors, you immediately notice displays filled with local crafts, salsa and chile powders, carmelized onions, dried fruit, breakfast cereals, spices, protein bars, soda pop, etc. These displays continue for quite awhile, making it easy to see what you need without wasting time searching for it. A few favorites: Their Domino's Pizza is good quality and just right, priced anywhere from 3.39 - 8.19 depending upon toppings selected. You may want to visit them after spending several days walking around, because they make great takeout! Also, try their canned Salsa Verde Chili, which comes in both mild and spicy versions. This stuff is incredible!!!! I would definitely drive across town again just to purchase this unique product. Grab a cobbler, pie, or banana pudding while you're waiting in line at Bakerella's Pastry Shop! If you've ever wanted to try burritos, now's your chance! Their Quesadillas and enchiladas come topped with anything from bacon to ground beef, cheese to sour cream, and rice to broccoli. When you order, ask for extra bacon if you plan to have the whole 'nother one to yourself! A little pricey, however...... but worth it in my opinion.

Stayed here in the spa suite for three nights. At first glance it looks swanky, but after spending half an hour in the room, you start to notice all these small irritations that seem to never get fixed no matter how many people stay there - like the mouldy peanuts on the bedside table and a broken tap which the hotel does nothing about because they charge 15 per use! The Bosphorus Suite is really nice though, with a great view of Istanbul's skyline (and at least the hotel gives away free newspapers from their own publication!) Check-in was very quick and easy as I arrived late afternoon. The helpful staff were happy to help me unpack my bags even before we checked out the next day. As mentioned by other reviewers, check-out time can be quite early: 11am or 10am depending on your booking type. We got access to our room 3pm, so had plenty of time left over despite being up until 2am checking emails while waiting for the tour bus to arrive (we spent one night in Beyoglu). In fact, we could have made do without the 4th floor balcony that overlooks the street outside the hotel, although this might not suit everyone if noise disturbance is important (it was noisy during some periods) and the hotel has bad wifi reception. There are two restaurants and bars within reach, and you cannot walk far along Taksim Square without coming across someone dining somewhere on a terrace. Overall, however, we loved our stay and will definitely return again. It was convenient to be close enough to Sultanahmet to visit the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia, whilst still having the quietness of the rest of the city nearby. Also good value for money.

I would definitely recommend checking them out because not only do they offer delicious food and fun atmosphere, but they truly care about their customers!

I was excited to find a sushi place near our home in Glendale, but the excitement faded as soon as I walked in to the place. The sushi rolls are made fresh right at your table so you can see how each roll is created right then and there! You're given tongs by the waitress to help open up the bamboo shell around the fish which provides a nice experience for someone who likes to actively create their food. The salmon one tasted like really good quality canned tuna and we loved everything about it except for the price point (14...what?!?) We also tried the Tuna Rolls that come on spicy rice crackers with an Asian dipping sauce and tossed with ginger dressing. Again, the sushi was gourmet-esque but nothing earth shattering or worth its 12-13 price tag. But overall, this sushi bar felt more expensive than any sushi joint I've been to in LA. So if you want to eat at the most Instagrammable spot in West L.A., you should check out Sushi GoGo.

That way, you can always leave extra food behind and take home a few more bites or even make a meal from there. You know those "to - go" boxes that McDonalds gives you? Well here they send 2 full size baggies with each item. No need to throw away bags containers! The service was excellent as well. We went during lunch rush hour so lineups weren't bad at all. In fact, our waitress said she'd never seen such large orders before. So yeah guys.... If you're looking for fast eats close to Stouffville, check this place out!:)

My husband and I wanted to try something new for date night and I've known about Bachi Burger for years through Yelp as one of the best burgers in Las Vegas. Bachi is located at the center of the Arts District with plenty of outdoor seating (with a gorgeous view) on their patio or inside if you're feeling too hot. The atmosphere was bustling when my boyfriend and I arrived around 7:30pm and there were no signs that this would be packed later into the evening. Once seated, the hostess came over and asked us what we'd like to drink which made me feel very welcome right away since she also greeted me by name even though I hadn't met her yet. She took down our order almost immediately without any hesitation and then we waited for our food. Although, I did notice they didn't seat everyone together once you ordered your meal; instead, each table got its own server who came over periodically throughout the meal to take orders and refill drinks. However, this wasn't a big deal during our visit because the staff always seemed busy keeping up with demand. The menu allows guests to build their own burger from scratch using fresh ingredients. My boyfriend ordered the signature onion rings seasoned with salt and pepper and paired them perfectly with his burger without overpowering either. For an appetizer before the burger came out, he went all out and picked the loaded fries - bacon ranch, green chile and cheddar cheese. They were crispy and delicious with just enough kick to satisfy him. All of these items are available on the side for only 1 extra per item, except for the chips which cost 1.50 more. Keep reading to see how much everything costs... With my dinner, I started off with the mac cheese bites (5). These bite-size pasta balls baked with Havarti cheese sauce and topped with parmesan cheese on top and panko bread crumbs on the bottom, make for an excellent snack or appetizer. Topped with Parmesan and Panko breadcrumb topping After our Mac Cheese bites my boyfriend opted for the steak frites sandwich truffle aioli (19). This featured grilled flank steak topped with bearnaise, served with toasted baguette for dipping. He said the meat was cooked well and there was plenty of flavor in the sauces. The sides were good - the beans and potatoes were cooked exactly the way he liked and the salad was refreshingly crisp. He actually loved eating steak for two dinners in a row! For dessert, I shared the apple crisper duet (10), which consisted of apple pie filling surrounded by vanilla ice cream. The crust on the pie filling was flaky while the ice cream was creamy like soft serve. Both flavors complimented one another, making for an extremely tasty treat. There wasn't anything wrong with this dish, although next time I might opt for a larger portion or add some nutmeg or cinnamon to spice things up a bit. Next, I tried the Buttermilk battered fried chicken leg quarters (12). Served with honey butter hushpuppies, delectable country gravy and applewood smoked bacon, the chicken tasted absolutely fantastic. The juicy pieces fell apart with just a slight touch of heat - perfect for people who aren't fans of super spicy foods! Our waitress brought water glasses filled full of ice for both of us and refilled them several times throughout our entire meal. In total, my back pocket bill after tip ran close to 55 without alcohol, and I definitely think this place can hold their own against other high end restaurants in town. Just don't forget to save room for dessert! Pairing them with other ingredients only enhances their flavor and adds complexity. My personal favorite spice blend is Jamaican Jerk. It makes great seasoning too, which is why I keep my freezer stocked year round.

The city also has some great museums including the Guggenheim and the Neon Museum as well as the famous Bellagio hotel that is featured prominently in "Casino," the movie starring Robert DeNiro about how the mob controls Las Vegas through legalized gambling. It was a very hot, dusty, smelly place down there with no air conditioning since most rooms have private balconies without AC units. But the hotels were still full. My first night we went out at 6pm and saw our first show - The Raging Idiots...a bunch of guys playing guitars, drums, piano, saxophone, etc., doing a sort of surfpsychedelic take on classic songs by The Beach Boys and the Beatles. Very cool! We then walked around downtown Vegas until closing time and found a free shuttle bus to take us back to the hotel where we crashed as hard as possible. We are now heading to Denver tomorrow morning for a few days before returning to Phoenix. This will be my last post until after July 4th weekend when I return home, leaving behind Austin and its wonderful music scene.

Most of us who live in Las Vegas have quietly accepted the fact that restaurants on the Strip are notoriously over-priced. It used to be that Strip restaurants offered a good value. A Strip restaurant didn't have to compete with the vast number of excellent restaurants that have opened in the last decade outside the city center. Today, that is not the case. As a food writer, I frequently eat out in Las Vegas. My criteria is simple: I want a high-quality meal at a reasonable price. When it comes to dining on the Strip, I have found that it is now usually more cost-effective to stay off the Strip. However, there are some exceptions. I recently had the pleasure of dining at Michael Mina's Seafood Restaurant at the MGM Grand. While the name of the restaurant suggests that seafood is the primary focus, there is much more to the menu. The restaurant also serves outstanding lamb, beef and chicken. Mina opened his first restaurant in San Francisco in 1993 and has been a presence in Las Vegas since 2006 when he opened Michael Mina at the Bellagio. At Michael Mina's Seafood Restaurant, the focus is on the freshest fish and seafood. The restaurant is set in a stunning contemporary space that features a dining room with chairs in blue, beige and gray as well as tables and banquettes in white and glass. The walls are lined with square-shaped tiles and illuminated by elegant chandeliers. We started with two cocktails: a Yellowtail Cosmopolitan (15) and a Pisco Punch (15). The Yellowtail Cosmopolitan was made with Grey Goose vodka, Cointreau, cucumber, yellowtail, lime and strawberry. It was a refreshing and delicious libation. The Pisco Punch is a Michael Mina's signature drink. The drink is made with Peruvian pisco, housemade pineapple and lemon juice, Angostura bitters, and prosecco. It is a bright and delicious cocktail. We followed with a round of appetizers: The 36-Hour Braised Beef Short Rib (18) is cooked in a red wine reduction, and served on top of house-made butter noodles and root vegetables. The short rib was fork tender and extremely flavorful. The Lobster Dumplings (16) are made with Maine lobster, shiitake, and black truffle, and served in a lobster bisque. These dumplings were a creative and successful dish. The Crispy Lobster Tacos (18) are made with Maine lobster, pickled jalapeno, avocado, and pico de gallo. I loved the fresh flavors of this dish. The 16-oz. Bone-In Prime New York Strip (58) is a 28-day dry-aged steak that is cooked to your desired temperature and topped with smoked tomato, and served with roasted fingerling potatoes and creamed spinach. This is a steakhouse quality steak. We also ordered the Pan-Roasted Colorado Lamb Rack (48). The lamb was served pink, with a Parmesan polenta cake, braised baby artichokes, and a mustard jus. It was a flavorful and perfectly prepared dish. The Chatham Cod (44) is a house specialty. The cod is served with crab, marrow-breadcrumbs, and a potato crepinette. The cod was moist and tender and the dish was a study in richness and flavor. The desserts are made in-house by the pastry chef. We ordered the Chocolate Cake (12), which is a rich and flavorful cake that is served with a milk-chocolate ganache and a chocolate sorbet. The Banana Tart (12) is made with caramelized banana, pecan streusel, vanilla ice cream, and toffee sauce. It is a lovely dessert. The service at Michael Mina's Seafood Restaurant is friendly and attentive. The restaurant is busy, but it is also well managed. The restaurant is open for lunch and dinner daily. It is also open for brunch on the week

My husband and I wanted to try something new for date night and I've known about Bachi Burger for years through Yelp as one of the best burgers in Las Vegas. Bachi Burger is a Japanese hamburger joint that originated in Tokyo and is known for their unique burgers. They are known for their famous egg burger, which we had to try. I have to say, it was one of the best burgers I've ever had in my life! I don't think I can ever go back to eating any other hamburger. I ordered the Tokaido-style burger with a fried egg, thick cut bacon and a ton of cheddar. The egg was perfectly fried and added a nice crunch to the burger and the bacon was also really good. The bread was so fresh and soft, it tasted like a bun from an Asian bakery. The burger was so juicy that it was dripping all over my hands and I just had to eat it with a fork because I didn't want to waste a drop of that burger juice. My husband ordered the Chicken Katsu burger. It was the first time he's ever eaten a chicken katsu burger. I was so happy to see that he really enjoyed it and he loved the sauce that came with the burger. We loved both our burgers so much that we ordered a dessert. We ordered the red bean mochi cake. It's a cake that's made from a Japanese cheesecake batter and filled with red bean paste. It was delicious! I've had red bean paste ice cream before, but never red bean paste inside a cake. The cake was very moist and it just melted in my mouth. The red bean paste added a nice creamy texture to the cake. Overall, I would definitely recommend Bachi Burger to anyone looking to try a new burger place. It's a good thing we don't live near one because I would be there everyday! Bachi Burger is located on the 2nd level of the Miracle Mile Shops in the Planet Hollywood.

I found my seat and settled in to watch the show. Fela! is the story of Fela Kuti, an iconic figure in Nigerian history. He was a musician and an activist who used his music to fight for political change. Kuti was a self-proclaimed Black President and a Pan-Africanist. He believed in freedom from oppression. In his own country, he spoke out against the Nigerian military government. He believed in equality and justice, but was not a pacifist. Fela and his followers clashed with the police. His mother, Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti, was a political activist and was killed when a Nigerian army truck drove through her home. He married twenty-seven women in one ceremony, because polygamy is a cultural tradition. He was jailed, beaten, and his house was raided and destroyed. He became an international figure and was known as a leader in the Afrobeat genre of music. The Belk presented the touring Broadway production of Fela!, directed by Bill T. Jones. It was a multimedia experience, with music, dancing, and video footage of the real Fela Kuti. The show was high-energy and fast-paced. The dancing and singing was fantastic. The production numbers were phenomenal. The band was on stage throughout the show. I had fun, but I have to admit that I didn't really understand much of what was going on. The show is presented in English and Pidgin English, but I didn't really understand the story. I'm not sure if the show was confusing or if I was just a little overwhelmed. The Belk has a large stage, and the action was moving all around. The staging and the use of lighting was amazing. There was so much happening that I couldn't keep track of it all. I'm not sure if I should go back and see it again, or if I should just let it go. I thought the show was interesting, but I'm not sure if I'll ever understand it. Bill T. I'm a spicy kind of guy in general. I love bold, intense, exotic spices. Those aren't the kind you find on typical grocery store shelves. That poses a dilemma perhaps? I recently attended an event where there was a sampler of six different chili peppers. There was also a sampler of various pepper jellies. Together, these two could create a true SPICY experience for the average palate. I thought about it. I took a few bites from each. I was actually a little scared. I've made dishes with a little bit of cayenne and habanero. I've used a pinch of cumin. This was like a whole other world. And I was the one who wrote a cookbook with a chapter devoted to spice! I was actually pretty paralyzed with fear. So, I did what I always do when I feel like I've taken on more than I can handle. I went to a cookbook to look for inspiration. I found something that sounded really good, and I adapted it for my own tastes. I have two versions of this recipe. One is vegetarian. The other is not. I think that this dish is perfect for a light lunch or dinner. It's colorful, bright, and delicious. Greek Yogurt. Greek yogurt is tangy and rich. Cumin. Cumin is ground, dried seed of a plant that grows in the Middle East. Garlic. Garlic is a plant that grows in the form of a bulb. Cilantro. Cilantro is an herb that is grown in many places, including Mexico and the Mediterranean. Ground Chicken. This meat is ground, cooked, and seasoned. Chili Paste. Chili paste is a cooked, dried, and ground chili pepper. 1. Start by warming the olive oil in a small saucepan. Add the garlic and chili paste, and cook until the mixture is fragrant, about 1 minute. 2. Whisk in the yogurt, cumin, cilantro, and salt. Keep whisking until the yogurt is smooth. 3. To make the chicken filling, combine the ground chicken, chili paste, garlic, cumin, cilantro, salt, and pepper. 4. Stir to combine, and form into eight 2-inch meatballs. 5. Add the remaining tablespoon of olive oil to a large skillet. Heat the skillet over medium heat. 6. Add the meatballs and brown. Turn the meatballs a few times to make sure they're browned evenly. 7. Add the lemon juice, and stir to combine. Cook the meatballs for about 1 minute. 8. Serve the meatballs with the chili yogurt. Add cumin, cilantro, garlic, and ground chicken to a large bowl. Mix to combine. Form the mixture into eight 2-inch meatballs. Add the remaining tablespoon of olive oil to a large skillet. Heat the skillet over medium heat. Add the meatballs and brown. Turn the meatballs a few times to make sure they're browned evenly. Add the lemon juice, and stir to combine. Cook the meatballs for about 1 minute. Serve the meatballs with the chili yogurt. I am so excited to try this. It sounds amazing. I was wondering if you could use a different chili or hot sauce instead of the chili paste. I don't know if I've ever seen that. I have not tried this with another chili or hot sauce! I would try to look for a chili paste that is made with cayenne, and see how it turns out. I think it might have a similar flavor profile. Good luck! I've made this recipe with ground turkey as well, and it's amazing! I actually doubled the recipe and made a small batch of the yogurt sauce, then froze half of it in an ice cube tray. Then I took one ice cube to make the sauce, added it to my stir fry, and voila!

Most of us who live in Las Vegas have quietly accepted the fact that restaurants on the Strip are notoriously over-priced. It used to be that Strip restaurants offered a wildly different dining experience than what you could find inside your local bodega, but with The Venetian's massive expansion and the opening of Caesar's Palace, things have become more commonplace across town - and it can feel like you're paying twice as much for less food (or worse, dessert). That all changed at The Kitchen this week when longtime Mardi Gras chef and restaurateur Stephen Starr opened his first Los Angeles location. In addition to offering an incredible menu of classic Southern cuisine that features dishes like shrimp and grits and catfish and gumbo so good they make everyone else's mouth water, this venture is part of a larger strategy for Starr. "I wanted to do something new here, create a place where people could really enjoy themselves," he tells SELF recently. That approach probably sounds familiar: He also founded a roughly 30-acre farm near his home in Virginia Beach earlier this year, which was eventually turned into an event venue called Plantation Farms. Starr has a passion for growing fresh produce not only because he appreciates its quality ingredients, but also because he believes it will help bring awareness to agriculture issues in America and promote environmental sustainability. "It's just my way of giving back," he says. "The kitchen is literally where I grew up - it was a big influence." That sentiment will definitely resonate with L.A.-based diners looking to get their fix without breaking the bank. To celebrate the grand opening of The Kitchen, we chatted with Starr about the launch of the first LA restaurant from one of the country's most prominent chefs, why he thinks there's still room to grow in Southern cooking, and how he plans on bringing this style of cooking to the rest of California. What inspired you to open the steakhouse? Stephen Starr: My family loves steak! We're very southern, and chicken or turkey is always the go-to for a meal. But a couple years ago we were sitting around the table one night listening to music, snacking on pizza rolls between every song as we watched our daughter play volleyball. And I said, "You know what, Stephen, maybe we should start eating better meals." And then she started saying, "Dad, what if you had some steaks?" So I thought, "Why wouldn't we? Let me try frying them or braising them and see how they taste." Then they became a regular thing on our dinner tables again. They've gotten so popular that now my wife and I cook three at a time, and we don't even serve the same ones anymore, so that's kind of cool. [Laughs] When my wife saw me come out with the idea of doing a steakhouse, she actually made sure that the cooking equipment came directly off of her dad's grill. She didn't want any shortcuts. Even though she's in charge, I'm still the boss, and the executive chef is just helping me run everything. How can guests enjoy these delicious meals without breaking the bank? STARR: Every night, we'll do a primo appetizer that comes with salad greens and a side of chips and salsa for 12.85. For dinner, we have a signature plate served from the bar for 39.95. We call it a Big Daddy, and it basically consists of two flat cuts of fine-grained Angus beef cut into 10 pieces each for grilled presentation. There's no charge for those plates; instead, we ask you to tip your server generously. Our Sunday brunch plates are 15 for 29.85 each. Those plates include breakfast favorites and some other savory items too, such as fried eggs Benedict. Also, we offer full portions of our famous housemade jambalaya (15), our signature red beans rice (6) and a variety of sides (spinach and cheese, potato salad, macaroni cheese, onion rings, etc.) Do you think we can expect more Southern restaurants to follow suit in L.A.? STarr: If you look at the places that already exist here, there's a real opportunity for more. Oh, and one of the reasons why we love doing lunch at The Kitchen is that it allows us to feed a lot more people in a smaller space. This place gives us almost 12,000 square feet to entertain in. You definitely need lots of space, but what we found is that different parts of the city are quite different. Downtown is sort of downtownish; Hollywood is more Sunset Boulevard-y; Beverly Hills isn't completely Beverly Hills; Midtown is filled with shops and restaurants; and Koreatown doesn't have walkable streets yet. They have a subscription service (not cheap) that lets you get a yearly pass which allows you unlimited use of all of their amenities including the pool area, sauna, steam room, etc.
They forgot my order, I waited 25 minutes for my bubble tea. The worst attitude I have ever experienced. Not even a smile from the staff...

This place sucks. The customer service is horrible. They dont serve food unless you order a pizza from a neighboring restaurant. Who does that? They dont control their crowd. Many of the games are just gimmicks...I play some, but most are lame and it seems like they have no interest in improving things at all. They do serve pizza, it's just not made by them.

Overall...a sensational effort. From the atmosphere (clean, stylish and modern...but not too cold or sterile) to the food (superb) to the service (attentive and knowledgeable staff)....the dining experience was a great success. Best wishes for future dinners! From the moment we arrived I felt like we had been taken care of by the staff at The Eden Terrace - they made us feel so welcome that we didn't even miss our flight back home until later in the evening. We were seated at an elegant round table immediately next to our friend from China who ordered a wonderful bottle of her favorite wine that night. There is also very little noise pollution when compared with other hotels around Excalibur- just enough to hear conversations outside but nothing overly annoying. They have created such a cool ambience; it's romantic and classic all at once. My only complaint would be about their rooms: while there are two large suites on this property, both of them require a separate entrance and you don't get much privacy. Also, considering that some of you may find yourselves staying longer than one week, I'd recommend reserving a room that has more beds rather than having your own private suite because the bedrooms here can get really crowded if guests choose to stay alone. As far as our meal goes, we started off the meal with champagne and creme de cacao before switching over to entrees which included the lobster bisque soup, most delicious ever and salmon fillet tartare with french fries. For dessert we tried the chocolate mousse fondant ice cream cone but found it quite unappealing. Unfortunately, our waiter did leave early after dinner due to his flight leaving shortly thereafter. However, he did call ahead to ensure that our meal, our bill, and payment (on credit card) would be complete without any issues. He returned late into the evening and said that everyone had enjoyed the meal although we weren't sure how many people actually stayed that long since others left earlier throughout the day. Overall, we highly suggest checking out the outlet shopping at The Eden Terrace where you'll find a variety of items for less money including designer clothing, shoes, jewelry, watches, luggage and accessories! Overall, another lovely experience at the World's Fair venue and a fun place to visit!!! We always enjoy going to this hotel and hope to return soon. It is conveniently located close to Universal Studios, Shops at Plaza Del Rey, and Hollywood Blvd. We visited several times last year during the holidays, and look forward to returning again. The space itself reminds me a lot of "my old high school house" and it feels kind of cozy and inviting inside. When i check in online, it says there are three rooms available (one bedroombathroom per person), however upon arriving, i spoke with the front desk agent who told me that all three rooms were available. When I asked what time it starts serving breakfast, she said that she couldn't say. She explained that guests should arrive between 8 am and 10am. This could have changed but my group got there first, along with my friend's family. We were treated nicely by a friendly and attentive staff member who took our order and immediately brought us water and coffee. Our room was comfortable (not luxurious, though). The bathroom was clean, sleek and well equipped for my needs. Breakfast was pretty decent. I think it's important for a hotel to offer something different every morning. On our second day, I went to the spa for a massage and it was super relaxing!!! All in all, The Eden's location makes it perfect for hotel stays. Plus, its brand new, chic design make it much easier to stay in shape AND relax. Most importantly, its price is fair according to the reviews and amenities. I definitely recommend this hotel!!

I've always liked Caesars but in the past year we've had 2 bad experiences. The last time I wrote and explained our issues with our room and the response was "that's what they're here for." But once again, that's a small percentage of their customer base and it could be my experience is different than others Fair enough I suppose if you can leave the resort, your trip will be much more enjoyable

The food: The reviews are true- the lamb kuzi is ridiculously good and a great buy. It is tender, well seasoned and very generous in proportion. They garnish with almonds which are not just tasty but they pack an earthy punch as well. These little bits of nutty goodness will become so familiar to you that soon your palette will be begging for more! Service: When it comes to service at this restaurant it's not just better than any other restaurant I've been too! The staff was extremely polite and helpful when we needed them. There were no queues or anything like that and the waiters were always friendly even if they weren't actually working. If you're looking for something really special then make sure you visit this place on a weekday evening because afternoons can get busy here.

This place is definitely fun. Like an upscale biker bar. That doesn't mean food is pricey at all. Generous helpings and good sides. Mac's is a good Charlotte staple. Macs not the best mac n cheese in town, but it's my personal favorite.

I was so hopeful to find a good BBQ place. I heard great things about this place but wanted to wait until the lines went down from it being new. Boy was my disappointment severely tempered by the fact that every time I saw this guy I couldn't help but think "what are you doing here? You obviously can't cook!"

I told myself that on my next trip to Vegas, I was gonna try one of the nicer buffets on the Strip. My husband I stayed at Paris, and it 's a great place for Asian food, but there were no buffets in our room... The first time we had tried to eat out of the hotel, we went onto Japans restaurant from the casino floor. The only thing wrong with that is they didn't have any of their own buffet items! They just picked some stuff off the menu and put it into a bag so you'd pay more. So when we finally got a chance to get away to another hotel where buffets allowed us to order all of our favorite dishes, I wanted to make sure I hit up Las Vegas Buffet Village. It's run by David Lee Heung who used to be an executive chef at Caesar's Palace. When we arrived at the buffet area area, there were about 30 tables set up lining both sides of the strip. We ordered our appetizers (a couple of appetizer platters), main courses (which were chicken wings, which tend to be spicy) and desserts (ice cream). Then we split our entrees between me, my husband and dessert (a chocolate covered cherry coke)! After all of this, it took us about 4 hours to finish everything, because I could not stop eating. This entire experience ranked right up there with what I would call "Hard Rides" - except this time, there wasn't a roller coaster or anything like that involved. Just 3 different kinds of Asian food. So, if you're looking for something new to do while you're visiting Vegas - check out Las Vegas Buffet Village! You'll definitely be glad you did!
This is a very well run airport, but the security line can get way too long. The food choices in the terminals is just ok. I agree with all of these points.

Worst place to go for medical care. Had me waiting for two hours for test results than when I finally get seen, I get the oh, we need to get you back to the hospital. Yeah that sucks! Do they have a specific doctor who does your blood work?

Even if you have been to a Bashas'markets Inc before, you must go to this one! You could spend hours here, eat dinner, have a drink, and shop. Obviously the most important thing is that you make sure all your friends visit it too. The one in the middle of Istanbul's Bosphorus? I don't think so...

I really try to be understanding about food taking some time. I am very willing to wait for quality food. Its actually my tagline for yelp...however, this place takes too long in the line and takes away from the real experience of being there. We sat at a table that was served as leftovers from yesterday's lunch. If it wasn't for the fact we were sitting next to a family with young children you would have no idea what they just ate. We didn't get any portion control either which meant our leftover food had enough calories to feed 10 people! The restaurant was clean and quiet when we arrived. The decor is very nice but not enough to compete with the other restaurants on this strip. It does however look like an upscale restraunt so I suppose thats why the service was slow. Note: My husband has been to this place before and they do take reservations....so if he comes back again let me know how many people are waiting because the place looks busy during lunch hours but is actually empty by dinner time.

Simple, well prepared food. Good atmosphere, good service. Heavier and more traditional than the meal we had at Bouillon Bilk the night before. We shared two bowls of soup with a choice of meat, fish or vegetable as each bowl came with one spoonful to start us off. I chose turkey while my girlfriend selected the chicken with rice option. It was all very simple, but it tasted fantastic and they were happy to share their anecdotes about the dishes that are made from scratch in-house by the chef. The staff would often look over your shoulder when you placed an order for different options - which really encouraged me to try some new things on our second visit. There wasn't much else to do around here apart from eating so it was great to get out of the city centre into something quieter. The restaurant is open Monday to Friday 11am - 4pm, Saturday 10am - 6pm; Sunday 12pm - 3pm. To find out additional information click here.

Food is decent. I ordered a stuffed trout dinner entree. Looks pretty good, a little bit cold. It was quite busy, which explains why they never fill up my glass and actually ask if you want it refilled! Sale is on now too for 10 off everything in the bar till 11PM daily until end of day Saturday night. Get there early as tables are limited to 6 people per table (wtf). The food menu sucks.. is just bread sticks with some meatvegetable tossed into them. Vicky I'm not sure what restaurant that "appetizer" is at but I thought it looked yummy! My friend went here last week and said it was really nice with plenty of things to choose from. They had sushi rolls an other side dishes so I think this place might be worth checking out if you like Japanese foods.

Never order Mexican with a slick facade. Anyplace in a strip mall with Grandma back in the kitchen usually yields the gold. This place, all hipster glitter and low rider leather, is just hipper than your average "hip" joint (in fact it's kind of old-school drenched in hippie accoutrements). The interior decor was more or less spot on for the neighborhood: lots of thin black lace curtains, red tablecloths. Not bad looking at all; not ghetto either. Inside, there are several bars one containing teens that slide open to reveal giant art installations hanging from the ceiling. A mannequin wears an Indian headdress and a woman goes shirtless while wearing what looks like a pirate costume. There were also some free service dogs wandering around but they seemed content to stay out of sight behind the glass partitioned off from the bar area and cubbies. They had no interest in eating anything and I'm pretty sure they weren't going anywhere near any drinks either. The food isn't as tasty as you'd hope considering the prices but man, do they have good appetizers. We went with the Mongolian beef roll (4) which was really quite good. It has chunks of meat in a poblano peppers sauce. My friend felt the same way about her burrito taco. That was our first taste into what we thought would be a typical 10-15 dollar meal (no joke), and boy was she wrong! She ordered a tostada but ended up splitting it with two buddies because it was so damn filling! Her buddy told me their meal came to over 35 dollars including tip before tax. While my burger wasn't as good, I got a nice steakburger topped with fries (9.95) basically a medium large fry served over lettuce and tomato. As mentioned above, the BBQ is actually being offered daily now everyday from 4pm - 9p.m. You can get the grill-topped chicken sandwich with a side salad for 85 cents per person, or the 7 dollar Tostada Combo. For this combo, you get two tacos, two cheeseburgers, two sides plus a drink. With the 4th of July coming soon though, don't expect much in the way of deals for 14.95 anymore. Next time you go take advantage of the Rib Time deal where they'll cut you a big piece of ribs and grill them on the grills outside if you want. But definitely enjoy every bite of your meal since this will probably be passed down through generations after yours.

We will not go back!! The ribs looked big and meaty but were tough. The Mac n cheese was dry and no flavor potato salad was the same. The pulled pork tasted like a burnt lumpy piece of pork with some sauce on it, very bland! I ordered extra fries to try them out as they always are so bad for you! We still had to eat all our food before we left I am going back soon because my husband likes it there. So the first time I went in is when they had that special outside on sale (taco night) for 12 price tacos 1 beer for people 21...

I would give Ginza 0 stars if I could! This was truly the worst dining experience I have ever had. My husband took me to Ginza for my birthday. Upon returning from breakfast, we were informed by a service representative that the restaurant is being closed down and they are not allowed to serve you anymore food or drink until further notice.... More

Stayed here in the spa suite for three nights. At first glance it looks swanky, but after spending half an hour in the room, you start to notice all these little things that make this hotel stand out from other hotels in Bangkok: -the bed is very comfortable and luxurious; -the bathroom has a stone counter top (no marble), which makes your skin feel refreshed; -their shower water is so hot that it feels like you're floating in the middle of a pool while soaking up some sun rays; -nice enough mini fridge with microwave Just wish there could be more space in the hotel The food was quite good, although I would have preferred it being served buffet style rather than sitting down at one end of a small table each morning waiting for someone else's breakfast. The staff were friendly and helpful, but not as attentive as they should be because "they are busy." Overall though great experience overall! Would definitely stay again

I got the veggie pad Thai- it was out of this world good. The tofu was delicious and the meal was chock full of vegetables. I love that they ask you what kind of veggies are in your order as opposed to just serving up whatever is on hand. The service was very courteous too. There weren't any problems getting a table, although there were only two people at our table when we arrived (one who mixed up the drinks which she apologized for later). The food was also very good. It came with an enormous helping of veggies, so if you don't want anything else around your dinner you can get plenty of variety and flavor from their menu. I definitely recommend going here!!

I bought Panda show ticket, Vegas.com stated that it comes with Gondola ride voucher but I didn't get the voucher and wasted few hours of my short vacation. At first, we thought we might not get back so quickly as we arrived at the casino in mid night. But after a bit more time, we started to see all of the people coming out from their hotel rooms (probably those who booked before our last day)

Great beer selection, of course. Had the Pork Belly sandwich and found it a bit too fatty, but taste was good. Their Potted Farm Egg appetizer was really good. Very nice service. Service was OK. Food came out promptly. A couple waitresses were not very helpful in finding others, so they weren't able to give me two for my husband (I thought he would want one). The bread that comes with the sandwiches is completely soggy! They need to get their act together here or be prepared to lose some customers... This is a new wine bar this summer along with one other which has been open for about three weeks now I think. It's neat because all the decor is vintage and woodsy decorated. There are quite a few seats that overlook the patio area where you can see North Park from. You order food to go and bring your own containers to put the food in after you have eaten. When we arrived on Saturday night for dinner we had no idea what we wanted but we ordered a pound of prime rib with garlic mashed potatoes, green beans, carrots, pears and creamed cauliflower. After eating our meal I realized it needed more meat and our waiter Daniel volunteered that there was a special order made which meant 40 pounds of beef were being delivered to them. So instead of ordering a second dish we got another 50 pounds of meat and had dessert. We also asked if someone could drive us around town a little as we didn't know that much about San Diego. Overall great experience and will definitely return.

Never really had a problem with this chipotle But had a terrible experience today. Employees were super rude from start to finish. Awful customer service. The lady at the end of the line behind me was so off her meds I wonder if she even knew what restaurant she worked in, or how much responsibility fell on her shoulders for serving people who apparently felt they could make food better than their own employees.... First of all It's Chipotle not Chippletts and secondly you should be ashamed that someone would treat you like that. That is definitely unacceptable behavior. You are right though this is not the first time I have seen something like this happen. My mom used to work there when it was chipper Toms and there were this one girl who always made sure everyone showed up and no matter how many times you showed up she still didn't believe you as well as other things happened behind the scenes. In my opinion it's completely unfair on them because some customers can't handle seeing your face instead of just hearing about it later when you come back into your car.

Siri took me here.... Take me to the closest Cigar Shop. I discovered there was so much more to this awesome inquiry! Walked into a Cigar experience. Pretty pretty nice.... The associates were friendly and helpful, Brand new products for sale... Smoking Experience. I did some research on their website and found that this place has been around since the 1920's.. So it is old school in many ways. They have also had other locations in the past.. At one point they used to be the "Cigarette Factory" but sold out to another corporation who changed everything about it. So I guess you could say the place is legit;)

I was excited to find a sushi place near our home in Glendale, but the excitement faded as soon as I walked in to the place. It has a very casual and grungy feel with lots of graffiti on the walls and the wooden floors are stained from years of use. The staff is not very friendly or courteous and it brings back memories of working at an upscale Japanese restaurant that closed down and left me feeling very disgruntled. Fortunately for my wallet, the Mermaid Sushi Bar does serve American food so I decided to go there. I realized quickly that this sushi place serves their authentic rolls (8-13) in pretty good quality. They have several different kinds of salmon, mackerel, tuna, halibut, sashimi tuna, shrimp, crab and more. I ordered my favorite roll, the Fuji Tiger Roll. This is a medium-sized roll filled with fried green tomatoes, cucumber, ginger, avocado, hot sauce, mayo and rice vinegar. You can also order your own toppings like scallions, seaweed salad, nori and tempura batter. My favorite part about these rolls are how much you get in one small package. You just pick up what you want which makes ordering a breeze! In addition to the rolls, they also offer two types of frozen fish bowls. One includes all ingredients including fresh salmon, sliced cucumbers, nori, nori chips, spicy mayonnaise, miso soup base, seafood seasoning and red chili pepper flakes. The other bowl features fresh salmon, chopped veggies, miso soup base, seafood seasoning, sesame seeds and a protein of your choice. Both versions cost 14.95 per person. The first thing that struck me when I entered the restaurant was the smell. This place smells like the old Japanese restaurants that used to be around especially during lunch hours. However, the food itself isn't bad. One plate of the Salmon Mackerel Roll that we had came out very crispy and juicy. There's actually no sugar coating here because everything is cooked perfectly. You get plenty of flavor without consuming any calories. Another plate of rolls arrived accompanied by some spicy miso soup based dish. Although the name of the soup describes what it tastes like, I really didn't taste any soup at all. Instead, it tasted like something salty, creamy and sweet. Alongside the soup, I had a bite of an appetizer called Grilled Salmon with Potato Bake. There were 2 pieces of cooked salmon (about 12 inch thick), grilled potato bake and chiles which added a lot of savory flavor to the otherwise bland salmon. I loved the combination of flavors and textures and would definitely recommend trying it again if you're ever visiting Los Angeles. Upon entering the restaurant, there is a menu posted next to each table featuring dishes such as Soba Noodles with Tuna, Helix Grilled Salmon with Broccoli Rabe and Salad, Shrimp Tempura with Grits and Cucumber and Truffle Crusted Salmon with Caramelized Onions. When I saw the prices the first time I thought "This place must be expensive!" But after reading through the menu again before making my selections, I felt a bit relieved seeing how affordable the meals seem to be. If anything, I now think these prices could perhaps make your meal better if you don't mind eating healthier options than you normally do. Mermaid Sushi Bar offers delivery via Uber Eats and DoorDash. For pickup orders, call between 11 am - 9 pm Monday - Saturday or email . The website also allows you to create an account online for easy checking out.

Really, you guys think chips should be the basis of a good or bad rating????? wow how about the actual food, the real meal, not the free stuff in front . You get 2 points for each item on your list (or maybe 1 per item) which totals out to 12 ingredients. The rest is just filler weight and excess packaging. It's like being paid to eat at McDonalds. that makes much more sense

Good service, good food, and great menu. By far better than Don Pedro's down the street. Come here quite often and every time food and service is great. I agree with this 100. The only downside on a busy night is that you have to wait for your table to get carried away by other people singing at the top of their lungs.

I really enjoyed my stay here. The entire property is very hip and comfy. The rooms are large with cool decor. The restaurant, Cafe ZuZu, serves great food and drinks. It's a short walk to the beach where you can get some nice seafood as well. We had a wonderful time! We stayed at Boulders in June of 2016. The location was perfect for us because we were visiting family on the island. A small drive from the town center but not far enough that it took away from the fun we were having. The house is clean, comfortable, and has everything that we neededwanted. There is plenty of room to play pool or other games while overlooking the garden out back. All in all I would definitely recommend this place if you're planning to visit St. Thomas. This was our second trip to St.Thomas, and both times we've rented a home here (prior to venturing off into the "big" city on vacation). This one was better than the first - spacious, cozy and decorated beautifully. The space would have been perfect for friends or families; unfortunately there was no room for 3 adults....BUT, we made do. The kitchenette was fully equipped for cooking your own meals, including an electric stovetop and microwave oven. There is also free WiFi access throughout the house so you don't need to worry about running into other guests online. Being only steps from the ocean, this is definitely a good option for those who like to spend their days relaxing by the water. Overall, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay and will definitely be staying again when we return. Mrs. Davis and her staff did a wonderful job of preparing and cleaning up after our family members' arrival. The 2 bedrooms were all nicely sized and quiet - perfect for two couples sharing. The outside area was landscaped and there's even a covered patio which seats 4-6 people. The dining table and chairs could easily seat 8 comfortably. I omitted to mention that the attitude stemmed from the fact that we did not have a local number, just the hotel's phone number. Apparently that was a problem for many of our guests and they complained about it in some way or another (from their point of view). I guess this is why you don't tell anyone where your room is beforehand! The service: The food at the restaurant was mediocre if I'm honest - sandwiches that had no taste and were probably the same thing twice on different days. Even though I was very hungry after being up all night, there wasn't much choice when I ordered my meal, which is supposed to be delivered to the room every morning. They didn't even bother filling out any paperwork with me when I paid my bill by credit card since apparently they're still the ones who control everything around here. You can watch them pack the tray into the car, but then let you take it home yourself instead of helping unload the u-haul van. Oh yes, and I forgot to mention how rude the waiterwaitress was - she kept saying "sorry" over and over again while serving us with the stuff required to make my sandwich. When I asked her about it, she said that she wanted me to feel bad so that's what she was doing. That was pretty disgusting tbh. Overall, I would say that Ramada Plaza Hotel Singapore is definitely worth visiting if you're planning a trip down south. Not only does it offer good value (for what it costs) but also has various amenities, including an outdoor swimming pool and free Wi-Fi throughout (which isn't available elsewhere in the city).

Happy to have a Jersey Mikes in Surprise, AZ. Been here 4 times and the have never disappointed! This location is extremely busy Yet, they are very good at working through the crowds." Read or Share this story:

My wife and I had breakfast here on a Monday morning before our flight home. We got seated immediately and had fast, happy service, and that's where the enjoyable portion of the experience ended," he wrote in his review posted to Trip Advisor. "The entire experience was thoroughly unpleasant (including the food). My first impression is that this place isn't made for tourists." That doesn't mean everyone else thought so. The restaurant has received five-star reviews from over 1,000 customers since it opened just last month. It also earned four-stars out of five stars by three other reviewers who visited in January.

First time! After asking some fellow YELPERS where do I go... they didnt point me in the wrong direction! the place is small. but I like that. makes me feel more at home and relaxed! They also have friendly staff who will be happy to help you (though not as much with luggage) or if needed, carry your bags. There are a few places downtown which offer similar services but without having to stow it all away behind a desk.

You got to get their carnitas grilled cheese with each bite, you know it was made out of love! The carnitas is so good, the melted cheeses delicious, and the lettuce wraps are my favorite!! My family thought this was a great snack for breakfast or lunch. It's not really low carb but very filling for dinner without many carbs. I wouldn't recommend using as an alternative to a waffle or other toast based on the amount of sugar in these wrappers - they're just better suited for eating straight from the bag than sliced bread. However if you want something low cal that doesn't taste like crap (like most low-carb snacks) then try this. They have some fattening mayo in them which isn't too bad at all when considering how much fat they slip right into but adding a tablespoon of sour cream can make it even more healthy:)

I don't usually write reviews but today I decided this place was worth one:) I just got the 12 piece chicken meal for the family and I have to say, it's a good deal. The chicken itself is cooked all the way through so you won't be disappointed with how tender the meat is! The sauce on top of that is delicious!! Like every other time we've been there, there are several tables set up in front of the building, so if you want a nice quiet spot to sit down, then make sure you do. Other than that, they offer some great appetizers (chicken salad anyone?), full breakfasts (eggs Benedict and pancakes), salads, sandwiches, soups, etc., as well as a couple other things here and there. We always order breakfast since my hubby has an early morning meeting and we always order fried eggs and hashbrowns or something like that. So far, our favorite is french toast. It's really yummy but not too sweet because it comes with vanilla syrup. If your kids ask you for brownies instead of french toast, go ahead and get them those! One thing I didn't mention about their restaurant is that they also sell homemade ice cream. Since Jason goes to church at our house most Saturdays during the summer, he doesn't mind stopping by and picking us up our frozen treats after service. They even make it themselves! Yum! Today we went over to the library at my parents' request. My mom had taken a class back in high school where she learned math skills (she loves numbers!)... I guess the class ran out of material but whatever. Anyway, when we walked into the library, we were surprised to find ourselves sitting next to this guy who looked like he belonged in a movie somewhere. He probably had some kind of gangster look going on with his long hair, beard, and yellow t - shirt topped off with black pants shoes. His eyes were grayish and brown but light blue around the pupil area.. No big deal right? Well, my dad said "Hey, I know him!" and told me what his name was. Hmmmmm.... weird. This guy started talking to me about our library card and asked if I knew any good books to read while I was at work that would help with my multiplication division problems. "Oh yeah," I replied. "That's The Hobbit." He gave me a goofy grin and I thought, "What book did you pick?" And then he said, "You're gonna love it." There was no hesitation from me and I turned to my dad and proclaimed, "YES!" So now I'm in The Hobbit and really enjoying it so far! It definitely isn't getting rated R yet because it hasn't gotten very violent, but it does contain a lot of gore and danger. Plus, the storyline is real interesting and makes sense (for a fantasy novel anyways). Once I finish reading the book, I'll post pictures of it here to let everyone else see for themselves!:) Ok, so I haven't posted anything in awhile and mostly it's because I haven't felt like doing anything. I think I mentioned before that my mom and I took my younger sister on vacation to visit her grandparents for the first weekend in July. Well, we had such an amazing time that it only made me want to stay home more. Like last week, we woke up bright and early, headed to Starbucks with the girls, sat outside and chatted for a few minutes before heading back inside to get ready for church. Afterwards, we headed straight to the zoo to watch some animals up close. During lunch, I brought out a cookie dough sandwich, which I made myself, and we both ate. Then we got a snack of chips and salsa from Walmart and headed to the aquarium. There is a huge tank filled with fish and some adorable turtles, plus aquarium exhibits, aquarium displays, tropical plants, etc. Now, the beach wasn't an option since it was too hot outside, so we settled up onto the beautiful grassy areas surrounding the pond behind the museum. After spending the day together, we drove straight home in the evening and crashed. However, I slept until 9am!!! Thanks to a lovely nap and lots of watermelon, my body feels better today than yesterday thanks to my sweet tooth craving! My husband and I wanted to try something new for date night and I've known about Bachi Burger for years through Yelp as one of the best burgers in Las Vegas. I always wondered what it would be like but never got around to trying it until last week, when we were out celebrating my birthday with friends. We went there at 7pm on a Thursday evening, right after a long day of work, and just before the restaurant starts to fill up from its late - night crowd. I was excited because this was going to be our first time dining inside of a Bachi Burger restaurant. The place is situated on the backside of the Strip near Aria and Caesars Palace hotels so you can see all the action down below if you're not seated directly above where they serve their signature bouchon burger. It's very close to Mandalay Bay too which makes it an easy stop off point or quick getaway destination during your stay in Vegas. Our table was next to the window overlooking the pool area behind us (you won't find that view anywhere else). In addition to the beef patty, we also ordered fries, onion rings, shake and a drink of choice. Bachi Burger takes its name from both the French word "boucher" meaning "to make" and veggie burger being veggie, the latter referring to the large portion size of the patty. As soon as we sat down, two guys walked over and introduced themselves: Benoit and David. They were working together at Bachi Burger when they realized they had worked together at a previous job a couple of blocks away called The Spot, but they weren't sure how long they'd still have each other on staff. Benoit was a greeters hostess while David served the guests. Their conversation started out light enough, about how they knew each other and then quickly turned into discussing their jobs; It turns out they used to do similar things at a local chain called Burger King. Together, they did everything from dealing with customers and managing barstools to cleaning tables and setting up food stations. David told me he remembered it took him three months to find another job since no one thought he could do anything better than at Batch Burger. He agreed with me that his current position at Batch Burger isn't exactly glamorous, but the thing I love most about him is how genuine he is. His smile, laugh and happy demeanor are contagious throughout the entire room. Inside of 30 minutes, David and Benoit had already established a friendship that has lasted several weeks, sometimes longer. There were many laughs shared between them and they even joked about applying for the same job a month later although one was on a higher salary and the other wasn't interested in continuing to work part time for less money. After about half hour, Dave offered to help out and take care of some dishes for us so we wouldn't end up having to pay an additional 5 per dish. Unfortunately for me, I didn't think about taking advantage of his offer until it was almost time to leave since I was quite tired from staying up too late the night prior. As soon as I saw him come towards me with a tray full of dishes, I knew he meant business. Dave finished serving us and requested that we tip him well considering the service he provided to us. Of course, I said yes and we tipped him pretty generously (10), leaving him with plenty of change for whatever else we needed to bring home. To keep in touch with each other once again after graduation, they decided to meet up for lunch on Friday and go shopping while we waited for our reservation at the Park MGM hotel. Since Batch Burger is now closed, it doesn't seem likely that they'll ever run into each other again, though it sounds great that they might continue communicating via phone calls and emails someday! I tipped him 20 but would never return again due his unacceptable service! - via Yelp The hardest part about traveling is figuring out where you want to eat next. There are so many different kinds of cuisine that each one has its own appeal. And as much as we love a good restaurant review written by someone who has actually eaten there, sometimes these reviews can be hard to take personally because they depict places in a negative light without ever having actually experienced them themselves...or even thought about them before writing their review. Here's some advice from people who have already traveled to several places that helped shape our eating style: Before you go anywhere - make sure to check the restaurants menu online (we like OpenTable), or ask your hotel concierge if your place has one. If you don't find one, then start searching for an alternative, similar to a recommendation on TripAdvisor; or book into a hotel near another favorite eatery and call ahead to see what's available. Once you've found somewhere you're willing to visit, you should also look around your neighborhood to see which other nearby spots serve similar dishes and expect to pay a bit more money than usual. Ask about their kitchen hours and if the wait time between meals is long. Some properties offer guests "mini-meals" when they arrive, typically consisting of two course lunch or dinner options. This may help keep costs low while ensuring you always have something to munch on during your stay. Also, do your research on parking pricing since parking is often included on this fee. Other common things to consider include whether they offer family dining plans (if you can bring kids) and what specialspromotions might be offered. Keep in mind that most hotels will charge extra if you decide to sit outside instead of inside, especially during prime springtime weather. Finally, try to choose places that focus on local ingredients rather than relying heavily on tourist staples such as sushi, steakhouse fare and fancy Italian cuisines. There's nothing wrong with a nice meal once in awhile, but when you go for it every night, it can become bland, monotonous and boring very quickly. In fact, to really live life well, think about going only three times per month and outside those three times. Don't stress too hard if the food isn't exactly on par with the best Michelin stars in town - just remember to enjoy yourself and all the little pleasures in life.

He told me that one day in December 2018 they had to shut down briefly after getting robbed twice, though sadly no guns were ever found. He thought the police would come back soon, "but not this month." That's a shame, considering how much money goes into making those shawarmas. A former Greek restaurant once owned by Gangemi brothers (above) closed recently due to understaffing. I spotted some open seats while waiting for our orders. The first thing we ordered was a large order of gyros (9). They are cooked fresh daily, including marinated chicken thighs stuffed with feta cheese. There really aren't words to describe the flavor of these shawarmas, which came covered in pita bread. They're crunchy yet satisfyingly chewy, and filled with delicious flavors like onion and garlic. My wife also liked hers well enough. For 10 each you can add fries or tzatziki sauce, too. And if you don't want any sides but only want chicken shawarmas...well then, yes please. I tried their baklava (8), too. A few holes poked through the golden pastry base. Not bad. But the best part of the dish has always been the refreshing gelato, and again, unfortunately, that didn't feel quite right here either. Maybe next time? They served housemade hummus (5), but not homemade falafel balls. Instead, instead of peppercorns, I saw dried herbs. Same ole, same ol' workin'. Their black bean salad (7) felt fine until I tasted it alone later. What a missed opportunity! We finished off with drinks: a plain Ouzo (3.50) and my favorite drink from anywhere else called the Mango Mojito (6). This combination of mango, lime juice and ice cubes will make your tongue roll around like crazy. We paid for ours since we know they do charging extra, which seemed weird given that alcohol sales have dropped dramatically everywhere over the past year thanks to COVID restrictions. Overall, it's nice to find another establishment offering great service without having to wait forever for anything to be ready. Of course I'm talking about Cafe Kebab Pizza Bar. You might never need to go out again!

My husband and I wanted to try something new for date night and I've known about Bachi Burger for years through Yelp as one of the best burgers in Las Vegas. When we were deciding on a restaurant, we both agreed that this was going to be our place. The decor is super casual yet chic with lots of greenery all around us which made it feel cozy even though my husband ordered a steak, mine was chicken. It's located right off of Flamingo Road so you always have your own private space there when dining outside! We started by sampling some appetizers like a cup cake taco or boba tea. I definitely recommend trying their homemade bacon bread pudding dessert if you're looking for an indulgence after dinner! Our main course came out first before anything else but once again, don't let the cute little menu fool you because they serve everything from salads and sandwiches to entrees. For me, since it was just the two of us, I chose the Kale Caesar Salad (pictured) and my husband had a Peking Duck wrap. My salad actually arrived pretty quickly while his took longer. Both items tasted amazing although having fresh kale instead of romaine lettuce would have been better. Our plating is beautiful too including the presentation box which holds your food really well during service, making sure your dish gets served perfectly every single time. The server brought out my Caesar salad to my table pretty fast along with my plate of fries but neither my husband nor myself looked at what was inside until later in our meal especially considering how delicious it was haha. We never expect restaurants to give us great tasting meals without any ingredients, vegetables, etc... Well yeah Bachi Burgers does not disappoint because the Caesar salad contained some of the freshest greens I have ever eaten, very flavorful, and surprisingly good portion size unlike most other caesar dressings I've tried. My favorite part being the pico de gallo sauce which added super flavor to the whole mix but also complied with my vegan diet needs. This was probably my second-favorite item in the salad bar aside from maybe another piece of their bacon bread pudding dessert but that's only because I didn't get to sample it: (As far as the burger itself goes, I say go big or go home. First thing I noticed about the burger while taking the picture was its size - oh boy did I underestimate their portions here. The porterhouse patty itself has more than enough meat for 2 people who are eating alone (which is rare). Although I'm usually not much of a fan of hamburgers due to how full I felt afterwards, this one was different because the way the toppings were placed on top gave a lot more room for me to enjoy it. One thing I wouldn't change however is the amount of ketchupmustard that was put onto each slice of cheese. That's gotta hit the spot, amiright? I loved the pears which helped balance out the large amount of ketchup that was used throughout the entire sandwich; it worked for me personally. All in all, if you love burgers then head over to Bachi because these guys know how to stuff them into your mouth lol - no pun intended:P

Around 7pm we finally settled on Flagstaff-hostels.com only after deciding against staying in downtown Flagstaff. We got 100 off an online rate which ended up being cheaper anyways than booking directly through their website (110 vs 150) So now everything was set! It took us less time to drive over there compared to driving 30 minutes to Grand Canyon National Park. We now knew where everything would be located if we did decide to stay longer. Mandalay Bay does not disappoint. Although I always stay at this hotel, this past weekend we tried one night at Mirage and 2 at MB - let me tell you that of all the hotels in Vegas, I'd have to say MB is my favorite...and it's good competition, too! This resort has an amazing view over the Las Vegas Strip from every room. In fact, the view was so impressive that when we booked our MGM Grand rooms a few weeks ago they upgraded us! Now we are on the 35th floor with incredible views of both the strip AND the mountains beyond (we're looking forward to spending time in Sun Valley next year). My husband said he didn't realize how much better these accommodations were until just now!!! Our first day here, while exploring downtown LV before dinner, we took several pictures along Fremont Street which overlooks the whole city including The Bellagio fountains down below....it really did feel like being in another world!! And as we got closer to The Venetian, we saw these big silver boats floating by...they had music playing while people walked around them taking pics...I thought those looked remarkably similar to the ones at Golden Gate Park in San Franciscobut there couldn't be more than 25 or 30 of them per boat.....so maybe it wasn't?? Anyway, as we approached, these guys came out to the middle of the street where we could see them and asked for tips. I'm sure the prices weren't exactly cheap but what do you think??? We figured why not give them some money?:) So with 20 we gave each guy 10 plus tipped him 5 because we felt bad about giving such small amounts...They seemed very gratefulwhich made sense since their job required walking up and down the Strip taking photos....Anyhow, back to Mandalay Bay....the view was really great even though it gets dark early here during wintertimeLike most folks who've been here...you can only get into the casinos after 5:00 PM typically. However, if you want to go to the GardensRancho Las Vegas area then you need to make reservations early! Our plan was to visit the Botanical Gardens nearby afterward..........However, we ended up staying late at Bally's instead great place with a large pool that looked like it would be fun right now! We had a nice meal at Grille 830 then went for drinks downstairs at Silver Dollar City bar called "Lucky......."and stumbled upon some jazz musicians doing covers of classic songs such as the Beatles' "While My Guitar Gently Weeps." It was great entertainment! The band consisted of 3 guitars bass player drummer......After the show we sat outside chatting awhile and watching traffic before heading off to bed. That's when the husband spotted something else interesting going on across the way a mini-golf course with apparently different kinds of holes to play depending how well your ball travels under water. What caught his eye was a hole marked "The World's Largest Waterfall"!!!! To our surprise, we found ourselves headed toward that water feature soon thereafter only to find no waterfall but rather huge pools filled with water with smaller streams feeding forth from rocks sticking up through the concrete on either side. Apparently, the official name of this pond is the Mojave River Pool and as someone pointed out earlier today, that should be a real attraction someday.........ha ha! Needless to say, we spent quite a bit of cash sitting inside the casino for two hours trying to sink a golf ball thru a hole measuring 4 x 10 feet????......felt weird standing still the entire time waiting to shoot the thing wasn't any kind of rush getting wet...anyway, once we finally finished the task, it paid off BIG TIME!!!!! Looked pretty cool hanging above the pool as seen here...I'll try to take a picture later tonight using my phone camera....hope everyone had a wonderful Thanksgiving Day and enjoyed their family gatherings! 5 comments: What an awesome experience you must have had!!! My first trip to the Belk was enjoyable, if a little confusing. I went to see the touring production of Fela! and parked in the parking structure, but it was closed for construction so my only option was the 4 shuttle bus that would take me out about half-a mile from where they were performing. The bus driver sounded like he had been doing this job forever (more than thirty years) without much training or direction on how to handle these situations; I could tell by his demeanor that he'd never heard of security rules when you aren't even working there. He kept making announcements that didn't make sense as we drove past major intersections with a lot of pedestrians everywhere - before turning left at some point, he told us not to park anywhere except along the curb because "the cops will come lookin" for the cars around our car while we wait behind them, then tried telling people who said stuff like 'we just have to get where we gotta go now' that no one else is going there any time soon anyway. The show started late due to technical problems and ended early due to rain storms all evening long which impacted everyone trying to leave after the performance. But once some patrons got home, decided they wanted to sleep instead of drive back up the hill, another group showed up demanding their money back. After awhile I sat down next to someone youngish whose ticket had fallen into her lap and she began talking to him. She eventually asked how old he was, gave him a ride off campus, and thanked him profusely. He looked quite fascinated by things African American culture - most likely raised in an area similar to mine somewhere south of Charlotte where folks are very proud of being black - and agreed to talk more later today over lunch together. Unfortunately he completely dismissed what I had been saying during class since technically speaking, he wasn't supposed to know anything about black race relations issues here other than the Confederate flag issue...much less any civil rights topic whatsoever that involves violence against blacks. It seemed clear though that something had happened to upset his family enough that he felt compelled to help strangers rather than running away screaming. As usual, when I stepped outside afterwards, I saw several demonstrators carrying signs protesting police brutality directed toward minorities...but also balloons filled with angry white kids hanging from utility poles between two apartment buildings. Apparently the balloon guy thought nothing of kicking them off to prevent further vandalism amid ongoing protests aimed largely at tearing down monuments honoring those who fought against slavery in the U.S., such as statues commemorating Robert E. Lee. You can find videos of people standing atop those same busts demanding justice for George Floyd and others still marching across America despite months of protests...with mostly negative results so far. I dunno why anyone thinks they're winning right now. And yet some continue arguingfighting until every last piece of property has been damaged beyond repair. And somehow I'm sure that's what Colin Kaepernick would think too: that "justice" should be served by everybody ending up dead. I couldn't imagine wanting to throw random objects onto a bunch of protesters risking life and limb, whether it's true that any lives really were lost or not. If having your personal property destroyed doesn't bother you anymore, I don't know if calling yourself part of society begins again either? Sure hope somebody comes through for the defenseless protestors someday.
